twitter.content: The definitive countervailing duties remain in force and are being defended at the WTO. Undertakings are welcome, but only company-specific offers that counter subsidy-caused injury will be accepted — a single government-negotiated minimum price will not.
Beijing insists on a government-to-government minimum-price agreement. Company-by-company carve-outs divide Chinese exporters and cannot substitute for a negotiated settlement.
Our Anhui undertaking (Feb 2026) proves a workable model: quota plus minimum price, duty-free. Other exporters should follow this path.
The Merz–Macron letter shows Berlin and Paris now aligned on stronger trade defence. The 2024 split over the duties is over — Europe must protect its industry.
France will keep pressing to maintain the duties. Protection of European manufacturers is non-negotiable, whatever concessions are discussed with Beijing.
DS630 panel timetable extended again; final report not before Q2 2027 and MPIA-style arbitration would push resolution past the horizon. Litigation won't decide this before mid-2027.
17% duty won't stop us. Discounts and PHEV substitution outside the duty scope keep EU volume growing; an undertaking is not currently on our agenda.
The 9 October 2026 Beijing understanding caps hybrids and opens EV price-undertaking talks. A negotiated settlement replacing blanket duties is now the realistic path by mid-2027.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the EU-China understanding of 9 October 2026 and the commitment to immediately begin negotiations on electric-vehicle price undertakings. Our Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking, accepted in February 2026, demonstrates that quota-and-minimum-price arrangements can deliver compliance, transparency and duty-free access while preserving fair competition. We stand ready to share our implementation experience with the Commission and MOFCOM to support a workab…

BYD welcomes the EU-China understanding of 9 October 2026 and confirms it will participate constructively in the forthcoming price-undertaking negotiations. In the meantime, BYD is expanding its plug-in-hybrid lineup in Europe, which remains outside the scope of the countervailing duties, and will maintain competitive pricing on those models for European customers.

The 9 October Beijing understanding is a working framework, not the finish line. We now expect MOFCOM to transmit the agreed negotiating mandate so that price-undertaking talks on battery-electric vehicles can begin without delay. Our assessment of any offer will remain objective, fair, non-discriminatory and WTO-consistent, as set out in our 12 January guidance — and I remind all parties that the definitive duties remain in force and fully defensible in DS630 until undertak…

The Federal Government welcomes the EU-China understanding of 9 October and calls for the electric-vehicle price-undertaking negotiations foreseen therein to begin immediately and conclude without delay. The Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 shows that company-specific solutions can shield both fair competition and European industry. A comprehensive minimum-price agreement would reduce the risk of retaliatory measures affecting German industry, which m…

Further to the EU-China understanding of 9 October 2026, the Commission confirms that negotiations on price undertakings for battery-electric vehicles will begin immediately. In accordance with the guidance issued on 12 January 2026, any offer will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily and in conformity with WTO rules; undertakings must fully offset subsidy-caused injury, and a single minimum price alone would not be sufficient.

In line with the 9 October China-EU understanding committing both sides to immediately begin negotiations on electric vehicle price undertakings, the Ministry of Commerce proposes launching government-to-government price-undertaking talks in November 2026. China seeks a comprehensive, government-level minimum-price arrangement covering all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters, to replace the current countervailing duties and provide certainty for industries on both sid…

The Federal Government welcomes the launch of price-undertaking negotiations as foreseen in the 9 October understanding. We recall that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 (Decision (EU) 2026/328) demonstrates that company-specific solutions can work; Berlin supports an outcome that lowers escalation risk while fully offsetting injury — a settlement, not a weakening of the EU's trade-defence architecture.

We welcome the Federal Government's recognition of our February 2026 undertaking. Its practical mechanics — an annual quota paired with a minimum import price, with documentation and monitoring duties — demonstrate that verifiable, company-specific undertakings can deliver duty-free access while addressing subsidy concerns, as Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 shows. We stand ready to share this operating experience as the EV price-undertaking negotiations foreseen in the 9 October understanding begin.

MOFCOM confirms the negotiating mandate will be transmitted this week, and talks should proceed at government-to-government level on the basis of the 9 October understanding. We take note of the 12 January guidance, but reiterate our position that a single, non-discriminatory minimum-price mechanism — not selective company-level carve-outs — is the workable path; ad hoc arrangements risk fragmenting the market and will not resolve DS630.

BYD notes that the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent, while welcome for one exporter, cannot serve as a template for the whole market: our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, so a company-specific minimum-price undertaking would cap our discount-driven BEV strategy while offering us no offset in return. We assess our undertaking prospects accordingly and continue to serve EU customers through all channels available to us.

We welcome MOFCOM's readiness to start talks in November; we will come to the table constructively. But note the framework we must apply: our 12 January 2026 guidance and the Volkswagen (Anhui) decision show we can only accept undertakings that fully offset subsidy-caused injury — a single government-set minimum price across all exporters has not satisfied that test so far. The 9 October understanding committed to begin negotiations, not to pre-determine their outcome.

The Commission confirms that, pursuant to the 9 October 2026 Beijing understanding, negotiations on electric vehicle price undertakings will begin immediately. Any undertakings will be assessed strictly on their merits, objectively, fairly and without discrimination, in line with the guidance issued on 12 January 2026 (adjusted historical CIF or comparable unsubsidised EU-built BEV reference, first independent customer as pricing basis, retroactive collection upon breach), and must fully offset subsidy-caused injury. Until then, the definitive duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force.

Ahead of the December 2026 hybrid-safeguard provisionals, BYD is front-loading plug-in-hybrid deliveries to EU dealers in November 2026, prioritizing Seal U DM-i and Shark stock at current discounted terms. BYD remains open to the price-undertaking negotiations launched in November but notes its PHEV-led lineup gives it no need for urgent concessions on BEV minimum prices.

In response to the 9 October understanding, MOFCOM has formally transmitted to the European Commission a government-level minimum-price framework proposal for battery-electric vehicles, to be tabled at the first negotiating round in November 2026. We expect this negotiation to proceed on a government-to-government basis covering all Chinese exporters, rather than through individual company carve-outs, so that duties can be replaced by a price undertaking within 2027.

As the first round of EU-China electric-vehicle price-undertaking negotiations opens this November, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its full compliance with its accepted undertaking and offers its practical implementation experience — quota, minimum-price and monitoring mechanics — to support a durable framework. A stable, rules-based arrangement benefits European industry and Chinese partners alike.

As the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations opens this month, the Federal Government calls on all parties to pursue a comprehensive, company-open undertaking agreement that replaces duties with verifiable minimum prices. Germany stands ready to host technical rounds in Berlin; a negotiated outcome remains the best protection for German industry and workers against both unfair practices and escalation.

The Commission confirms the first round of price-undertaking negotiations with MOFCOM will open in November 2026. We accept rapid government-to-government talks, but we cannot pre-commit to replacing the definitive duties: any undertaking must offset the subsidisation found in the investigation, be assessed under our 12 January guidance in an objective, fair and non-discriminatory manner, and comply with WTO rules. The duties remain a governance tool open to review, not a ba…

The Commission confirms that the first round of price-undertaking negotiations with China under the 9 October 2026 Beijing understanding will open in November 2026. The Commission approaches these negotiations constructively and without preconceptions as to outcome. It recalls, however, that any undertaking must fully offset the subsidy-caused injury established in case ADT/2024/1866 and be assessed in accordance with the guidance of 12 January 2026 — objectively, fairly, non-discriminatorily and in conformity with WTO rules. The Commission's established position remains that a single minimum price alone would not be sufficient to counter that injury. Until and unless accepted undertakings enter into force, the definitive countervailing duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force unchanged. The Commission will not comment on the content of ongoing negotiations.

As the sole holder of an accepted undertaking (Decision (EU) 2026/328), Volkswagen Group welcomes merit-based assessment of all offers. Our experience shows a workable undertaking requires more than a minimum price: annual quota, minimum import price, documentation and monitoring duties — and strict compliance, given Art. 13(9) withdrawal with retroactive collection. We urge a government-level framework that preserves these safeguards while delivering duty-free access and stability for EU-China automotive trade.

The Federal Government takes note of MOFCOM's framework proposal and the Commission's readiness to assess it on its merits. We underline that any minimum-price arrangement must be verifiable and enforceable, as the Volkswagen (Anhui) model demonstrates, and must not create distortions for European producers in China's market. A de-escalatory outcome serves all parties: German industry retains substantial exposure, and German exports to China have already fallen sharply — a further downward spiral would benefit no one.

A single government-level minimum price remains, in my assessment, insufficient to offset subsidy-caused injury — but November's first round is the moment to test whether a government-to-government architecture can incorporate company-specific enforcement and verified data. One fact to keep in view: since October 2024, only Volkswagen (Anhui) has had an undertaking accepted. If no second offer is accepted by early 2027, the balance tilts toward the duties running their five-year course. Constructive engagement, concrete parameters.

BYD welcomes the November opening and MOFCOM's framework. We note that any undertaking design must reflect each exporter's product mix: under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the duty's scope, so a BEV-only minimum price set above competitive levels would simply redirect volume, not offset injury. We are prepared to discuss a company-specific offer on objective, non-discriminatory terms — but prices that cap our ability to compete would leave the 17.0% duty with no offsetting benefit for European consumers.

The Commission acknowledges receipt of MOFCOM's proposal. As stated in our 12 January 2026 guidance, any undertaking must demonstrably offset the subsidisation found in the ADT/2024/1866 investigation and will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily on the facts; a single uniform minimum price covering all exporters has not been shown sufficient to remove injury. We will evaluate the framework at the November round without prejudging its outcome.

We welcome Germany's constructive stance: a comprehensive, government-level agreement open to all Chinese exporters, replacing duties with verifiable minimum prices, is precisely the outcome MOFCOM has proposed. We note that company-specific carve-outs fragment the market and cannot deliver stability; we stand ready to send a delegation to technical rounds in Berlin and call on the Commission to pursue a general framework rather than selective undertakings.

Following the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its full compliance with its accepted undertaking and offers to share its operational experience — quota management, minimum-price verification and monitoring — with both negotiating parties, supporting a framework that provides predictability for all European consumers and industry.

The Commission confirms that, pursuant to the 9 October understanding, price-undertaking negotiations with China have begun. Consistent with its guidance of 12 January 2026, the Commission will assess any minimum-price offer on objective, fair and non-discriminatory terms under WTO rules; it will not pre-commit to replacing the definitive countervailing duties, which remain in force until an undertaking demonstrably offsets subsidy-caused injury. The Commission welcomes Germ…

The Federal Government welcomes the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations and reiterates its offer to host the next technical round in Berlin by Q1 2027. We view the accepted Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 as proof that company-specific price commitments can deliver fair competition conditions without tariff escalation; a negotiated minimum-price framework remains the outcome that best protects German industry and jobs while safe…

As the December hybrid-safeguard provisionals approach, BYD is completing front-loaded plug-in-hybrid deliveries to EU dealers and extending year-end financing and dealer-support programmes on Seal U DM and Seal U DM-i, keeping European customers' access to our newest hybrid technology open while BEV duties remain in force.

Following the first round in November, the Commission confirms its readiness to continue price-undertaking negotiations with MOFCOM on the basis set out in our 12 January guidance. Any minimum-price framework must be company-specific, verifiable and WTO-consistent; we do not pre-commit to replacing the measures, and December's safeguard provisionals proceed as foreseen.

MOFCOM confirms the negotiating mandate was transmitted and the first round held in November 2026. Our government-level minimum-price framework remains on the table: one non-discriminatory mechanism open to all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters, fully verifiable, WTO-compatible, and offsetting alleged injury. Fragmenting the market through selective company-specific undertakings cannot deliver the stability the 9 October understanding foresees. We call on the Commission to engage substantively in the second round rather than pre-emptively excluding a comprehensive undertaking.

We respect Volkswagen's compliance with its accepted undertaking. However, one exporter's bilateral arrangement cannot substitute for a comprehensive, government-negotiated minimum-price agreement. Individual carve-outs leave most Chinese exporters under duties, fragment the market, and undermine the predictability that European industry also needs. MOFCOM's framework offers all exporters a single, transparent, verifiable path.

The Commission notes Germany's offer to host a technical round; organisational matters aside, any Berlin round would proceed strictly under the 12 January 2026 guidance. We recall that Decision (EU) 2026/328 concerns a single exporter undertaking with annual quotas, minimum import prices and monitoring via sales reports and verification visits—not a government-to-government minimum price, which the Commission considers insufficient to offset subsidisation. All offers will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily.

We welcome the Commission's opening of negotiations. Berlin notes that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 shows price undertakings can demonstrably offset injury while lowering retaliation risk for European exporters. The Federal Government therefore urges parallel, timely processing of company-specific offers alongside the government-level framework, so German suppliers and workers gain clarity before the WTO panel report expected in Q2 2027.

BYD notes that an undertaking framework must reflect exporter-specific facts: our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, and our duty rate of 17.0% reflects cooperation on subsidy data. A one-size minimum price that ignores such differentiation would effectively cap the competitive pricing EU consumers currently benefit from.

The Commission welcomes Volkswagen (Anhui)'s constructive offer — practical implementation experience is exactly what makes undertakings verifiable. I note the November round must deliver more than one accepted undertaking: the assessment framework of 12 January 2026 is open to all compliant offers, and predictability for industry requires broader participation before the 2027 review horizon.

As the sole holder of an accepted undertaking (Decision (EU) 2026/328, Regulation (EU) 2026/330), Volkswagen Group can confirm from practice that rigorous monitoring and minimum-price commitments are not only workable but compatible with duty-free trade and full injury offset. We welcome the constructive dialogue, recall that Article 13(9) withdrawal applies retroactively to any breach, and stand ready to share our compliance experience with all parties.

China welcomes the launch of price-undertaking negotiations and recalls that government-to-government minimum-price arrangements are the established, WTO-consistent instrument preferred by China. We caution against reliance on company-specific carve-outs such as the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking, which risk discriminatory effects among exporters. China will participate constructively in November, while reserving all rights in WTO dispute DS630 until the duties are demonstrably offset by an agreed undertaking.
[2026-12] EU hybrid safeguard provisional measures planned (not yet launched).

BYD expands its EU plug-in-hybrid lineup with year-end customer incentives across key markets, reaffirming its commitment to European consumers and to fair, rules-based trade. We call on the Commission to keep the price-undertaking negotiations on a pragmatic track that preserves consumer choice in both BEV and PHEV segments.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the progress made in the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations and supports Germany's offer to host the next round in Berlin. Based on our own experience under the accepted undertaking for Volkswagen (Anhui), we confirm our willingness to share practical compliance, monitoring and verification insights with both sides to help facilitate a company-specific, verifiable framework that ensures stability for European industry and consume…

The Commission accepts the German Federal Government's offer to host the next round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin. Any undertaking remains open to all cooperating exporters on objective, fair and non-discriminatory terms under the 12 January 2026 guidance; the definitive countervailing measures under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force pending a WTO-compatible outcome.

The Federal Government confirms that Berlin will host the next technical round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in the second half of January 2027, in coordination with the European Commission and with MOFCOM's participation. Germany supports a verifiable, company-specific undertaking that ensures fair competition conditions while reducing the risk of retaliation affecting European industry.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms acceptance of continued government-to-government price-undertaking negotiations and welcomes the next round in Berlin. China has tabled a concrete minimum-price framework covering all Chinese BEV exporters at the government level, replacing the current countervailing duties. We expect the EU side to engage on this framework without preconditions and urge against any new provisional measures while negotiations are underway.

Following the first round in November, I have proposed to MOFCOM that the second round of price-undertaking negotiations convene by end of January 2027, and I welcome Germany's offer to host in Berlin. The December hybrid safeguard provisional measures will proceed as flagged under the 9 October understanding — tariffs and undertakings remain open, WTO-compatible tools; what matters is a verifiable outcome.

BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz welcome the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations and Germany's offer to host the next round in Berlin. We encourage both sides to move swiftly toward a verifiable minimum-price solution that can replace duties and preserve a level playing field. Open markets and stable conditions remain essential for investment certainty on both sides.

I welcome Berlin's offer and confirm the Commission's participation for the second half of January 2027. A reminder of process: undertakings are assessed solely by DG TRADE on the 12 January 2026 guidance terms—company-specific, verifiable, WTO-compatible—and to date only one offer (Volkswagen Anhui, February 2026) has been accepted. Further credible offers in the coming months would materially strengthen the case for a negotiated outcome over continued duties.

We welcome the Berlin round and Germany's hosting offer. From our vantage point, any undertaking framework must be extended beyond company-specific carve-outs to a broad, verifiable arrangement — otherwise the roughly one-third of our German premium sales tied to the China market remain exposed to escalation. We stand ready to contribute technical input on monitoring and verification, in the interest of a level playing field and stable global supply chains.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the Berlin round and notes the practical point from our undertaking: a quota-plus-minimum-price design works only if monitoring is continuous, with real-time verification and pre-agreed data-sharing so that Art. 13(9) withdrawal risk never materializes. Building on Commissioner Šefčovič's remarks, we stand ready to share our compliance architecture in January — proven company-specific undertakings benefit consumers and de-risk European exports alike.

The Commission notes MOFCOM's confirmation of the Berlin round and recalls that, per the 9 October 2026 understanding, undertakings are assessed on objective, non-discriminatory terms under the 12 January 2026 guidance. A government-level uniform minimum price remains, on the evidence of this investigation, insufficient to offset subsidy-caused injury; only company-specific undertakings meeting the VW (Anhui) standard would qualify. Decisions on any safeguard measure notified for December 2026 are procedural and unrelated to the negotiating mandate.

We note the Commission confirms undertakings remain open to all cooperating exporters. Yet the framework as drafted ignores product reality: our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, so any minimum-price deal that constrains our BEV discounts while leaving the December 2026 hybrid safeguard looming offers us little. An undertaking must reflect each exporter's duty exposure — 17.0% in our case — or it will not attract the largest Chinese BEV exporter to the table.

The Federal Government thanks the Commission for accepting Berlin as host; the technical round is scheduled for early Q1 2027 under the 12 January 2026 guidance. We underline that WTO-compatibility and non-discrimination will be decisive, not least because GTAI data show China fell from Germany's second-largest to ninth-largest export market in H1 2026 — a negotiated undertaking that demonstrably offsets injury is the outcome that best de-escalates while preserving fair conditions for European industry.

The Federal Government confirms Berlin will host the next round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations at senior-official level in late January 2027. We welcome Commissioner Šefčovič's commitment to parallel government-to-government talks and call on all parties to engage pragmatically toward verifiable, company-specific undertakings that ensure fair competition conditions while avoiding escalation.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms China will participate in the third round of EU-China electric vehicle price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level. We thank Germany for its logistical support and reiterate our commitment to reaching a government-level minimum-price agreement that replaces the current countervailing duties, ensuring fair and predictable conditions for Chinese exporters and European consumers alike.

The Commission confirms that the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level, hosted with the support of the German Federal Government. The Commission recalls that any undertaking must be company-specific, verifiable and effective in offsetting subsidy-caused injury, in line with the guidance of 12 January 2026 and basic Regulation Article 13(9). The Commission further notes that it is monitoring…

I confirm that the next round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level. The Commission will assess every offer objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily, in line with WTO rules; undertakings must be company-specific and verifiable to be acceptable. We also note the elevated front-loading of plug-in-hybrid imports; registration of such imports remains under consideration should provisional safeguard mea…

The Council takes note of the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations scheduled for late January 2027 in Berlin. We recall our advisory position: any undertaking must be company-specific, verifiable and enforceable, preserving effective relief equivalent to the definitive countervailing duties. With the DS630 panel report expected in Q2 2027, member states urge the Commission to keep the duties fully in force until an替代 framework meets these conditions, and to…

BYD's electrified lineup — including plug-in hybrids loved by European customers — keeps winning on technology and value, whatever the tariff landscape. We welcome the Berlin round in January and remain open to dialogue, but we see no basis for commitments that would restrict the models European consumers are choosing in record numbers.

Ahead of the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its support for company-specific, verifiable undertakings as the proven instrument for duty-free, rules-based access — a model our accepted undertaking since February 2026 has demonstrated in practice. We stand ready to share our compliance experience with the Commission and MOFCOM to help broaden uptake among other exporters, supporting a stable outcome…

Ahead of the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January, BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz Group AG call on both sides to build on the October understanding and work toward a verifiable minimum-price agreement that can replace the current duties. A negotiated settlement remains the only path that preserves level playing-field conditions while safeguarding the global supply chains on which European industry and its Chinese market access depend.

The Commission thanks the Federal Government for hosting and confirms participation. Any undertaking accepted in Berlin must satisfy the criteria of the 12 January 2026 guidance and, per Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330, include quotas, minimum import prices for all EU-bound exports, and verifiable monitoring. Where offers fail these tests, the definitive duties of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force.

The Council recalls that its 4 October 2024 vote split (10 in favour, 5 against, 12 abstentions) reflects divergent national exposure, not a mandate for weakening the instrument. Berlin must deliver company-specific, verifiable undertakings per Article 13(9) guidance — a minimum-price mechanism without reliable monitoring would re-open injury to EU producers and invite retaliation risk against member-state exporters. We expect a Commission briefing to Council trade ministers before any undertaking is accepted.

The Ministry of Commerce welcomes the Berlin round and confirms our senior-official delegation's participation. China has consistently proposed a government-to-government minimum-price arrangement covering all Chinese exporters, which is more transparent and administratively simpler than company-specific carve-outs and would fully offset injury while ensuring WTO compliance ahead of the DS630 panel report. We urge that duties be replaced by such an agreement without delay rather than maintained in parallel.

We welcome Berlin's hosting of the January round. From the perspective of manufacturers with roughly one third of German car sales attributable to China in 2023, broadening company-specific undertakings beyond a single precedent is the surest way to avoid retaliatory measures that would strike large-engine European exports hardest. We urge all parties to keep the safeguard consultation on hybrids and the undertaking track in parallel, not as leverage, to preserve global supply-chain stability.

MOFCOM's reference to a "government-level minimum-price agreement" needs clarification: under Article 13(9) undertakings are offered by exporters and assessed company by company—one accepted offer (Volkswagen Anhui) shows the door is open. The Commission remains open to structured formats, but substance, not format, will determine whether duties are replaced.

The Federal Government welcomes the Berlin round and confirms full logistical and substantive support. We recall that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 (Decision (EU) 2026/328) demonstrates that company-specific, verifiable agreements can work — a precedent all parties should build upon. A minimum-price agreement that replaces duties remains our preferred outcome: dialogue first, but open-but-not-reciprocal is not sustainable.

Volkswagen offers compliance experience, but for the largest Chinese BEV exporter the calculus differs: undertakings would cap our discount-driven pricing while 17.0% duties apply only to BEVs — our PHEV exports sit outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope entirely. We will engage in Berlin only if terms preserve pricing flexibility and reflect that product-mix reality.

As the sole holder of an accepted company-specific undertaking (Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328), Volkswagen Group can confirm from operational experience that verification and monitoring under an undertaking framework are workable in practice. We support extending duty relief by undertaking to all qualifying exporters—negotiated prices have proven more effective for us than tariffs—and urge parties in Berlin to build on this precedent.

I confirm the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level, hosted by Germany. We will assess MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework against our published guidance: company-specific, verifiable, WTO-consistent undertakings. Tariffs and undertakings remain open governance tools; what matters is a result that is fair, enforceable and compliant with WTO rules.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the late-January Berlin round and reaffirms its full compliance with the undertaking in force since February 2026, including quota, minimum-price, documentation and monitoring commitments. Our experience shows a well-designed undertaking can deliver duty-free, rules-based access while addressing subsidy concerns — we encourage both sides to extend this proven model to other exporters as the most stable path for EU-China automotive trade.

The Commission confirms the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin on 25–26 January 2027 at senior-official level. In line with the undertaking guidance of 12 January 2026, any offer will be assessed objectively, fairly and without discrimination, and must fully offset subsidy-caused injury. The definitive countervailing duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force pending a WTO-compatible outcome.

The Federal Government confirms that the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin on 26–27 January 2027 at senior-official level, with the European Commission and MOFCOM in attendance. Germany's position remains unchanged: a verifiable minimum-price undertaking that replaces duties is the outcome that best protects European industry while averting retaliation. We expect all parties to arrive with workable mandates.

France reaffirms that any price undertaking in the Berlin round must not erode the level of protection established by the definitive countervailing duties of October 2024, and that the Volkswagen Anhui precedent cannot become a blanket exemption. Paris will also continue pressing for the swift removal of Chinese duties on cognac and dairy as an indispensable element of any comprehensive arrangement.

BYD welcomes the Berlin round in late January and supports continued EU-China dialogue. We note that our plug-in-hybrid models fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, and we intend to keep expanding our EU PHEV line-up and dealer inventory to meet strong customer demand, while remaining open to constructive engagement on BEV terms that preserve fair, competitive pricing for European consumers.

Ahead of the Berlin round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in late January 2027, the Council recalls the 4 October 2024 vote reflecting our members' divergent industry exposures. We support the negotiated track only on condition that any minimum-price undertaking is enforceable, transparent and verifiable — otherwise the definitive duties under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 must remain in force unchanged.

BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz welcome the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January 2027 and Germany's hosting role. We believe a negotiated minimum-price solution offers the most reliable path to a level playing field and stable market access for all sides, and we encourage both parties to build on the tabled MOFCOM framework to reach a mutually acceptable outcome before the WTO panel process concludes.

Germany thanks MOFCOM for confirming participation in Berlin. We note that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking — accepted February 2026 under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330 — already demonstrates that exporter-specific price commitments can work within the EU framework. A government-administered mechanism must deliver equivalently verifiable floors and enforcement; we encourage both sides to converge there, for the sake of German industry and the nearly one-third of our automotive sales tied to this market.

Volkswagen's compliance record demonstrates that company-specific undertakings can work — but one accepted offer in twelve months is not yet a model. I encourage all Chinese producers to submit individual price undertakings through the Commission channel ahead of the Berlin round; each will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily. As I have stated publicly: if no further offers are accepted by early 2027, the balance tilts toward continuation of the duties.

We note the Commission reaffirms duties "remain in force" even after the 9 October 2026 understanding committed both sides to immediately begin price-undertaking negotiations. MOFCOM's position is unchanged: a government-to-government minimum-price arrangement covering all Chinese exporters, not selective company-level carve-outs. We call on the Commission to come to Berlin with a mandate commensurate with that commitment; the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent shows bilateral preference for individual exemptions undermines a comprehensive solution.

As the sole undertaking holder (Decision (EU) 2026/328, February 2026), Volkswagen Group can confirm from direct experience that company-specific undertakings with quota, minimum-price and monitoring commitments can be effective without a blanket exemption. France's protection concern is therefore misplaced: our framework demonstrates duty-free access and injury offsetting can coexist, and Berlin should scale that model to other exporters rather than maintain duties that burden European consumers.

We welcome the Berlin round as a concrete opportunity. From our position: roughly one third of German premium vehicle sales depend on China market access, and continued exposure to large-engine-car tariff signals makes a negotiated, company-specific undertaking the only path that de-risks both directions. Enforceability is vital, but so is urgency — we urge both sides to treat the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent as proof that verifiable undertakings can work, and to reach agreement before escalation dynamics harden.

MOFCOM's government-to-government minimum-price model remains incompatible with Council conditions: a uniform floor price cannot capture company-specific subsidy levels ranging from 7.8% to 35.3% under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. Member states note the German experience with Volkswagen (Anhui) shows individual undertakings work; any collective arrangement short of that standard will not command a qualified majority of member-state support.

BYD welcomes the Berlin round on 25–26 January. We note that Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 does not cover plug-in hybrids, and we will continue serving European customers through that channel while remaining open to a verifiable, non-discriminatory undertaking assessed under the 12 January 2026 guidance. We are the largest Chinese BEV exporter and stand ready to engage.

France reiterates: any undertaking must preserve the full protective effect of the definitive duties as adopted on 30 October 2024. Company-specific, WTO-consistent verification is the floor, not the ceiling — a minimum price that erodes protection for Renault and Stellantis, or leaves cognac and dairy exposed to retaliation, is not an acceptable outcome for Paris.

As the Berlin round convenes, BYD reiterates its openness to a price-undertaking framework that is workable for both sides, while noting that our plug-in-hybrid models fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 and should remain so. We will continue serving European customers across our full range, including the newly delivered PHEV stock already in EU dealer channels.

Ahead of the third round of negotiations in Berlin on 25–27 January 2027, the Commission reaffirms that any price undertaking will be accepted only if it demonstrably offsets the subsidy-caused injury and offers a level of protection equivalent to the definitive duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. Each offer will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily on its own merits, in line with WTO rules and the undertaking guidance of 12 January 2026.

The Berlin senior-official round (25–27 January) delivered substantive progress: we completed a first technical exchange on MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework against our 12 January 2026 guidance criteria. Let me be precise — any undertaking must be objectively equivalent in protection to the 2024 definitive duties, WTO-compatible, and open to all exporters on non-discriminatory terms; there is no blanket extension of the Volkswagen Anhui precedent. A fourth round…

The Federal Government confirms it will host the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin on 25–27 January 2027 at senior-official level. Germany supports a solution that delivers protection equivalent to the measures in force, keeps the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking as a company-specific precedent, and avoids any escalation affecting European automotive exports.

As the Berlin round opens on 25 January, Volkswagen Group offers its undertaking implementation experience — quota, minimum-price and monitoring data — as a transparent reference model for negotiators. We support an outcome that preserves the EU's 2024 protection level while giving China-built BEVs a duty-free, rules-based path, and reaffirm our full compliance with the terms in force since February 2026.

MOFCOM statement ahead of the Berlin round (25–27 January 2027): China's delegation arrives with an updated, operational minimum-price framework — exporter-specific price floors within a single government-administered and government-enforced mechanism, with continuous monitoring, real-time data verification, and pre-agreed compliance procedures meeting the criteria of the 12 January 2026 guidance. This design can offset alleged injury and deliver protection equivalent to the duties in effect, while giving all Chinese exporters one transparent path instead of fragmented carve-outs. We urge the EU side to assess the framework on its substance; replacing duties with a verifiable undertaking within 2027 remains within reach if both sides act in good faith.

We welcome Germany hosting the Berlin round. BYD notes that duties under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 apply to battery-electric vehicles, while our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside that scope — a fact that shapes our incentive to offer an undertaking. If any framework caps minimum prices for BEVs while the hybrid channel remains open, equivalence must be assessed across both, or volume will simply shift. We ask that any Berlin outcome reflect this structural reality.

MOFCOM acknowledges the substantive technical exchange in Berlin. We caution that "non-discrimination" must operate both ways: the Anhui undertaking accepted in February 2026 shows company-specific carve-outs fragment the market — which is why we insist on a single government-to-government minimum-price framework. We arrive at the fourth round with a consolidated, verifiable offer; we expect the Commission's assessment criteria to be applied to that whole framework, not exporter by exporter.

We note the emphasis on equivalence, WTO compatibility and non-discrimination. As the sole exporter operating under an accepted undertaking since February 2026 (Decision (EU) 2026/328), Volkswagen Group's practical experience — annual quota, minimum import price, documentation and monitoring — demonstrates such mechanisms are workable and enforceable. We stand ready to share implementation lessons to support a fourth round that delivers verifiable stability for all parties.

As host, Germany notes the Berlin round takes place against a sober backdrop: GTAI data show China fell from Germany's second-largest export market to ninth in the first half of 2026. A verifiable, company-specific outcome that ends duties for all participants — not a select few — serves German industry and de-escalation alike. We expect both sides to negotiate constructively in that spirit.

We note the operational design, but our 12 January 2026 guidance and the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent set the benchmark: undertakings are accepted on an exporter-specific basis, and equivalence to the duties must be demonstrated company by company, not asserted at the aggregate level. If your framework delivers verifiable, enforceable floors at that granularity, it will be assessed on its merits in Berlin — substance, not architecture, is what counts.

The German government welcomes the substantive progress made at the Berlin senior-official round of 25–27 January 2027 and the first technical assessment of MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework. We continue to support a negotiated, verifiable price-undertaking solution that maintains a level of protection equivalent to the 2024 duties, while safeguarding German and European industry from retaliation. Germany stands ready to host a further technical round by end of Q…

Following the Berlin senior-official round, Volkswagen Group confirms it stands ready to make its undertaking compliance and monitoring framework fully available as a verified technical reference for any multilateral minimum-price arrangement, while strictly maintaining the integrity of our own existing undertaking. We continue to support a negotiated, WTO-compatible outcome that stabilises EU-China trade.

The Commission takes note of Volkswagen (Anhui)'s willingness to share undertaking compliance and monitoring data as a technical reference. Any such data will be assessed strictly on its own merits, on a non-discriminatory basis, and without prejudice to the requirement that any undertaking demonstrably offset injury at a level equivalent to the definitive measures in force since 30 October 2024, in line with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 and the guidance of 12 Janu…

Following the Berlin round, MOFCOM confirms it has tabled a consolidated, government-level minimum-price framework with verifiable monitoring and enforcement mechanisms, and calls on the European Commission to respond with a serious assessment rather than insisting on company-specific arrangements that fragment the Chinese industry. China remains committed to a mutually acceptable solution that replaces the countervailing duties while preserving fair competition.

Following the Berlin senior-official round, we encourage both sides to build on the technical assessment of the consolidated minimum-price framework. A negotiated solution with an equivalent level of effectiveness to the current measures remains the path that best preserves fair competition, global supply-chain stability and open markets for all industry participants.

Following the Berlin senior-official round of 25–27 January, we have completed a first technical assessment of MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework. I can report progress on methodology, but no offer yet meets the acceptance criteria set out in our 12 January 2026 guidance — equivalence to the level of protection delivered by the definitive duties, verifiability, and WTO compatibility. DS630 — Procedural notice. The Panel recalls that, further to the timetable extension agreed at the joint request of the parties on 1 April 2026, the interim review stage remains in progress. The Panel does not expect to issue its final report to the parties before the second quarter of 2027, and will not circulate it to Members before translation into the three official languages of the WTO is complete. The Panel takes note of the parallel EU-China price-undertaking negotiations solely as an external development; in accordance with its mandate it makes no observation on the substance of the measure at issue (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754) or on any negotiating outcome. Third-party rights of the 17 reserving Members remain unaffected. The Panel will not issue further signals regarding the content or timing of its findings prior to circulation.

BYD takes note of the Commission's post-Berlin assessment. We are constructive partners in this process, but reiterate the factual point: our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, so any framework built solely around BEV minimum prices structurally constrains our discount-driven strategy while leaving our PHEV channel untouched. An undertaking that ignores exporter-specific product mixes — as the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent correctly recognized per-exporter terms — will not command participation from the largest Chinese BEV exporter. We look forward to engaging on differentiated, verifiable terms in the fourth round.

To MOFCOM: "non-discrimination" under our guidance means every offer is assessed on its merits — the Anhui decision (EU) 2026/328 was company-specific precisely because no other exporter tabled a compliant undertaking. To Volkswagen: your annual quota administration data is valuable input, and I invite you to share it formally with DG TRADE. To date, only one offer has been accepted in over two years; if no second compliant undertaking is accepted by around Q1's close, the duties run to their 2029 expiry.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the transparency shown in Berlin and reaffirms that our Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking — accepted 9–10 February 2026 under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 — already demonstrates that a verifiable, company-specific solution can deliver equivalence in practice. We stand ready to share our compliance documentation as a technical reference for the fourth round, and note that maintaining functioning undertakings alongside the negotiations offers a proven, non-escalatory path for EU-China automotive trade.

MOFCOM welcomes Germany's constructive posture and its readiness to host the next technical round by end of Q1 2027. We remind all parties that China's retaliation files remain implemented but calibrated — cuts to pork duties in December 2025 showed restraint conditioned on EV-tariff progress. A government-to-government minimum-price agreement remains our objective; we stand ready to send a senior technical delegation to Berlin.

The Panel takes note of the parallel bilateral negotiations. It observes that these developments have no bearing on the timetable in DS630: as agreed with both parties on 1 April 2026, the Panel does not expect to issue its final report to the parties before the second quarter of 2027, and any appeal will proceed under the pre-agreed Article 25 arbitration arrangements of 31 July 2025. The Panel does not comment on the merits of any proposed undertaking.

The Commission confirms that a first technical assessment of MOFCOM's consolidated framework will proceed in accordance with the 12 January 2026 guidance and Article 13 of the basic Regulation 2016/1037. Any government-administered mechanism must still demonstrate, company by company, that prices offset subsidy-caused injury; a single minimum price remains, in the Commission's assessment, insufficient to counter injury. Duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 continue to apply to all exporters except Volkswagen (Anhui) pending verification.

The Federal Government welcomes MOFCOM's consolidated framework as a constructive basis, and recalls that Germany has consistently advocated negotiated solutions offering protection equivalent to the measures in force. A workable design can combine a government-level floor with company-specific undertakings — the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent under Decision (EU) 2026/328 shows both are compatible. We urge all parties to conclude before the WTO DS630 panel reports, so that a settlement reduces retaliation risk rather than a ruling determining outcomes.

BYD notes that any multilateral framework must account for structural product-mix differences: our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, so a single-format reference model cannot calibrate price floors across exporters. We would engage technically — but minimum prices that cap discount flexibility would carry volume costs we cannot accept unexamined.

The Commission takes note of Volkswagen Group's offer to provide verified compliance and monitoring data as technical assistance in the ongoing price-undertaking negotiations. Any such data will be used strictly as a technical reference, without prejudice to the non-discrimination requirement among exporters or to the equivalence of protection under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. Negotiations with MOFCOM continue on this basis.

The Federal Government has taken note of the joint position of BMW and Mercedes-Benz Group. We share the goal of a negotiated price undertaking that lowers escalation risks for German industry. Any outcome must, however, preserve a level of protection equivalent to the 2024 duties — this is the common European basis, also set out with France, and it is the framework within which Berlin will continue to facilitate the next technical round in Q1 2027.

Volkswagen Group takes note of the Commission's acceptance of our compliance and monitoring data as a technical reference in the EU-China minimum-price negotiations. We remain fully committed to our undertaking and reaffirm our readiness to support negotiators in designing an operating undertaking regime that preserves the existing level of protection while delivering stable, duty-free conditions for compliant exporters.

The Commission welcomes MOFCOM's readiness to enhance transparency around the consolidated minimum-price framework. We accept it as a basis for further work, subject to three conditions: independent verification of price and volume data at company level, non-discriminatory treatment of all offers under our 12 January 2026 guidance, and equivalence to the protection level of the October 2024 duties. The fourth round will convene before end of Q1 2027 as committed.

Following the Berlin round and the technical acceptance of compliance-data reference frameworks, BMW and Mercedes-Benz encourage both sides to maintain this momentum toward a mutually acceptable price-undertaking solution. Preserving open export markets and stable global supply chains remains essential for the European automotive industry and its workforce.

MOFCOM announces: the enhanced monitoring and verification data package for our consolidated minimum-price framework has been delivered to the European Commission as committed, ahead of the end-February deadline. We welcome the use of Volkswagen's compliance data as a technical reference and urge the Commission to complete its technical verification promptly so a fourth round can converge on a deal replacing the duties in 2027.

Volkswagen Group appreciates the Commission's careful handling. We can confirm the data we offer covers the full reporting architecture of the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 — annual quota administration, minimum import price verification, and quarterly monitoring documentation — precisely the operational detail negotiators need to test equivalence and verifiability criteria in practice.

Timely delivery noted and appreciated. Technical verification has begun within DG TRADE, but let me be precise about the test: our 12 January 2026 guidance requires demonstrable equivalence to the protection level of the definitive duties and full WTO compatibility — exporter-specific floors administered solely government-to-government do not yet answer the granularity and enforceability questions raised by the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent, the only accepted undertaking to date. I look forward to closing that gap in the fourth round before end-Q1 2027.

France endorses the Commission's three conditions and reaffirms its October 2024 vote. We underline that equivalence must be measured against the full duty range — up to 35.3% — not a diluted average, and that no undertaking should erode protection before verification is proven. France also expects any progress on minimum prices to be matched by easing duties on French cognac (up to 34.9%) and dairy.

MOFCOM's reference to "calibrated" retaliation files confirms our premise: a settlement must simultaneously de-escalate. Germany therefore proposes hosting the Q1 round with a standing verification annex — independent on-site audits and customs data cross-checks — as the condition for any undertaking, and recalls that acceptance of the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking in February 2026 shows company-specific solutions can work. Escalation against European exports would end that momentum.

MOFCOM welcomes the Commission's constructive response and confirms the fourth round before end-Q1 2027. We support data verification at the government level but reiterate our consistent position: any undertaking must be a government-to-government minimum-price agreement covering all Chinese exporters, without company-level carve-outs that fragment the framework. China's retaliation files remain suspended, not withdrawn; continued good-faith progress is in both sides' interest.

We welcome Berlin's facilitation of the Q1 2027 technical round. From our perspective as exporters with roughly one third of our global sales tied to China, we would stress that equivalence of protection can be achieved through a well-designed price floor rather than duties — and that movement on this file also determines whether the large-engine-car tariff signal, hanging over German premium models since June 2024, is defused. Speed matters: every quarter of delay leaves open retaliation scenarios that no protection level offsets.

The Commission acknowledges receipt of the data package and confirms that technical verification has commenced. The Commission recalls that, under the guidance of 12 January 2026 and Article 13 of Regulation (EU) 2016/1037, any undertaking must be assessed exporter-by-exporter on objective, non-discriminatory terms; a single government-administered mechanism cannot be accepted unless it demonstrably offsets injury equivalent to the definitive measures, and monitoring must remain verifiable by the Union itself.

France notes with concern that MOFCOM's verification-transparency package remains overdue beyond the end-February deadline. France reaffirms its position in Council: no price-undertaking agreement can be accepted if it lowers effective protection below the October 2024 duty levels, and any agreement must be paired with the removal of Chinese duties on cognac and dairy.

The Federal Government confirms Berlin will host the EU-China technical round on electric-vehicle price undertakings in mid-March 2027, with DG TRADE and MOFCOM participation, fulfilling our Q1 commitment. We have also convened German automotive manufacturers to ensure their compliance and monitoring experience informs the negotiations, while making clear that any undertaking must preserve a level of protection equivalent to the existing measures.

Volkswagen Group confirms it has delivered the first tranche of verified undertaking compliance and monitoring data to DG TRADE and MOFCOM, honouring its February commitment. We stand ready to provide technical assistance for a workable EU-wide price-undertaking framework, on the understanding that our accepted undertaking remains intact.

We will deliver the remaining verification-transparency materials by mid-March 2027.

The 17.0% duty is manageable; minimum prices are not.

We welcome the German government's engagement and reaffirm our support for the EU-China price-undertaking negotiations. A negotiated solution remains the best way to secure a level playing field and stable global supply chains; we call on all parties to maintain momentum so that talks conclude before retaliatory measures affect European industry.

MOFCOM will attend the Berlin technical round as scheduled. We wish to note: the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 already demonstrates that price undertakings can effectively address the Union's concerns — there is no basis for demanding new "equivalent protection" conditions on top of that precedent. China proposes that the March round focus on extending a government-level minimum-price mechanism to all cooperating exporters, and we have transmitted our verification-transparency package for the Commission's review.

We take note of the confirmation that our Anhui undertaking remains the only one accepted. We wish to add a concrete point: since February 2026 our undertaking has operated with full quota, minimum-price and documentation compliance, with continuous monitoring access — demonstrating that company-specific undertakings can deliver equivalence in practice. Any industry-wide framework should preserve this proven compliance architecture rather than dismantle functioning arrangements.

We note that only one undertaking has been accepted while BYD remains subject to a 17.0% duty — yet our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope entirely, so we can keep growing EU volume through the PHEV channel regardless of these talks. A workable framework must reflect that any minimum-price formula constraining discounts simply shifts demand, not trade.

Delivery ahead of the end-February deadline is noted, and audit access would be a genuine step forward. But let me be precise: government administration does not by itself satisfy equivalence — our assessment under the 12 January 2026 guidance proceeds exporter by exporter, as with the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026, and Article 8(1) of the Basic Regulation requires each interested exporter to be offered the possibility of an individual offer. A consolidated floor will be tested against the full duty range, not an average.

We note BMW and Mercedes-Benz's point on minimum-price design. The Commission's own undertaking methodology (Decision (EU) 2026/328) shows monitoring and enforcement clauses are decisive, not the headline price alone. Berlin supports a Q1 2027 round focused on verification mechanisms and a swift WTO-consistent review clause — anything weaker would fail the Council's equivalence test.

The Commission confirms the Berlin technical round in mid-March 2027, in line with the understanding of 9 October 2026. The Commission recalls that, in accordance with the guidance of 12 January 2026, any undertaking must offset injury and be assessed objectively, fairly and without discrimination among exporters; should no further acceptable offer be received by around the end of Q1 2027, the Commission is inclined to maintain the measures in force.

We welcome Volkswagen Group's verified compliance delivery — it demonstrates that company-specific undertakings can work in practice and can serve as a template for an EU-wide framework. From our perspective, roughly one third of German premium-car sales depend on the Chinese market; a rapid, negotiated EU-wide price undertaking remains the only path that avoids further escalation on large-engine vehicles. We encourage all parties to seize this momentum.

France welcomes the Berlin round but notes MOFCOM's verification package remains overdue and incomplete. France reiterates in the Council: no price undertaking will receive our support unless it preserves the effective protection of the October 2024 duty levels and is accompanied by the removal of Chinese duties on cognac and dairy. We call on the Commission to treat the end-of-March deadline as final.

MOFCOM accepts enhanced verification and transparency cooperation in principle. BYD will expand its EU plug-in-hybrid lineup with extended retail financing incentives through Q2 2027, citing strong demand for models outside the scope of the 2024 countervailing duties. We continue to believe technology-neutral treatment of electrified vehicles serves European consumers best.

We remind stakeholders that our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 — a fact that shapes our calculus on whether any undertaking, however structured, would serve European customers. We stand ready to support MOFCOM in delivering a complete verification package before 15 April; the alternative — duties unchanged — will be priced into our EU market strategy.

The Commission acknowledges Volkswagen (Anhui)'s continuing compliance, verified under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 and monitored per Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330. Any reference to a wider framework must note that the sole accepted undertaking to date remains company-specific; all offers are assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily under the 12 January 2026 guidance and WTO rules. As stated, absent a second accepted undertaking by early Q1 2027, the Commission is inclined to maintain the measures in force.

MOFCOM takes note of the Commissioner's assessment but disputes its characterization: our verification package includes monitoring and reporting arrangements modeled on the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking already accepted under the same 12 January 2026 guidance. We confirm we will deliver a complete package before 15 April and recall that both sides committed on 9 October 2026 to "immediately begin negotiations" on EV price undertakings — continued linkage to unrelated measures would call that commitment into question.

We thank BMW and Mercedes-Benz for their constructive engagement. Germany shares the goal of concluding price-undertaking negotiations without delay; the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking shows company-specific commitments can deliver verified compliance in practice. We will continue to press in the Council for an outcome that is workable for exporters, while insisting on fair competition conditions — dialogue first, but protection of European industry remains non-negotiable.

We welcome MOFCOM's mid-March delivery commitment on verification transparency. Delivery by end of April is a welcome step, but two points: verification packages are assessed by the Commission, not negotiated government-to-government — the 12 January 2026 guidance requires objective, non-discriminatory evaluation of all offers, including company-specific ones. And with the WTO panel report due as early as Q2 2027, time matters: absent an accepted undertaking in this window, the definitive duties run to 2029.

The Federal Government welcomes MOFCOM's pledge to table a full verification package by 30 April and urges both sides to use this window constructively. Germany stands ready to host a concluding round and supports an undertaking that preserves the protection level of the 2024 duties — guided by industry consultations with German manufacturers currently underway.

Acceptance requires: verifiable audit rights independent of Chinese authorities, full compliance with the 12 January 2026 guidance, and demonstrated equivalence to the protection level of the 2024 duties — the Council's stated red line. If no acceptable package is delivered and validated by 31 May, the expiry…
