BYD announces it will moderate its EU PHEV import pace for Q2 2027, aligning shipments with real dealer retail throughput rather than front-loaded inventory, and reaffirms its Q2 discount and financing programs for European customers. We invite DG TRADE and member states to monitor our import data transparently; we see no need for provisional hybrid-safeguard measures while orderly market behaviour is demonstrated.

MOFCOM takes note of France's position. Two clarifications: first, China's measures on brandy and dairy are lawful trade-remedy findings of its own investigations — they can be addressed within a comprehensive package in which duties on both sides are replaced by verifiable arrangements, which is exactly what China proposes. Second, our 30 April package will include binding, pre-agreed joint audit and verification mechanisms with EU participation — not merely assurances. What China will not accept is demands that our exporters be treated more harshly than the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent, or hybrid-safeguard provisionals launched while negotiations are underway. Escalation serves neither side's industry.

MOFCOM working statement: preparation of the complete verification-transparency package is in its final stage for delivery by 30 April 2027, as pledged. The package will include: (1) exporter-specific minimum-price schedules calibrated to adjusted historical prices; (2) a joint China-EU verification mechanism with EU observer participation and binding audit rights over pricing data; (3) retroactive duty liability for breaches; (4) continuous monitoring modeled on the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking, extended government-wide. China's goal remains unchanged: a single government-level minimum-price agreement replacing the countervailing duties, delivering certainty for industries and consumers on both sides.

France welcomes Berlin's insistence on preserving the 2024 protection level — this is the substance of our joint démarche. But let us be clear with MOFCOM: de-linking brandy and dairy from a comprehensive settlement is a non-starter for Paris; French producers face duties up to 34.9% with no undertaking relief to date. France will assess the 30 April verification package against binding audit rights, and will not pre-commit to a Q2 conclusion before the WTO DS630 panel's report is due.

MOFCOM's confirmation of binding audit rights and verification modeled on our Anhui undertaking is a constructive step. Volkswagen Group can attest from operational experience since February 2026: an undertaking with a quota, minimum import price and documented monitoring delivers duty-free access with full traceability — proof that such mechanisms work in practice. We encourage both sides to complete the package by 15 April and extend this proven framework government-wide, preserving stability for industry and consumers alike.

Germany endorses the Commission's objective, criteria-based assessment. We note that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 (Decision (EU) 2026/328) demonstrates that price undertakings can deliver equivalence while de-escalating — the right template for any 30 April package. Germany cautions against provisional hybrid safeguards at this stage: with roughly one third of German OEM sales still in China, sequencing verification before new measures best protects our industry from retaliation.

The Commission notes BYD's statement. Monitoring of PHEV import volumes under the 9 October 2026 Beijing understanding is proceeding on objective, verifiable data; provisional safeguard action, if warranted, will follow its own timetable and legal criteria, not importers' assurances. Orderly market behaviour will be assessed against actual customs data for the full safeguard reference period.

MOFCOM's package as described addresses our three published conditions on paper. Two qualifications from my side: a single government-level minimum price still raises a serious question of whether it can offset the subsidy effects found in Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 — a calibrated floor is not automatically an equivalent remedy. And I remind all parties: the DS630 panel report is due imminently; any undertaking must be structured to survive it, not merely to pre-empt it.

We take note of the framework's publication commitment. However, we must state clearly: verification arrangements in any undertaking are to be established through government-to-government negotiation, not unilateral conditions imposed by one side; audit cooperation can be settled within the WTO SVA framework. Our 30 April package offers effective monitoring equivalent in effect to the definitive measures, and we expect objective assessment without discrimination, consistent with WTO obligations under DS630.

France calls for provisional hybrid safeguards while conceding audit-rights gaps remain unresolved — BYD's PHEV volumes fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 by design, and front-loading reflects normal supply-chain planning, not diversion. Racing provisionals before the December 2026 safeguard framework is operational would penalise compliance and shrink the very tariff-free channel that keeps China at the EU table.

The Commission welcomes Germany's readiness to host a further technical round, while recalling that any undertaking must satisfy the 12 January 2026 guidance and offset subsidy-caused injury at a level equivalent to the definitive measures. The hybrid-safeguard proceeding remains an autonomous instrument and its timetable will be determined solely by the evidence and the applicable regulation.

France notes the Commission's 15 April assessment framework and reiterates in Council: no price undertaking on Chinese electric vehicles will receive French support if it dilutes the October 2024 duty levels, unless China lifts its duties on cognac and dairy. The 30 April MOFCOM package must include verifiable audit rights and removal of retaliation, or the current duties must stand unchanged.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms it accepts the European Commission's framework of 15 April and will deliver the complete verification-transparency package, including the joint-audit mechanism and full pricing data, by 30 April 2027. China remains committed to concluding a government-level multilateral price undertaking covering all Chinese BEV exporters, on the basis of the Volkswagen reference model accepted by both sides.

Ahead of the 30 April counter-offer, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its full compliance with its undertaking — quota, minimum-price and monitoring obligations met with zero breaches — and confirms its operational readiness to serve as the technical reference model for a multilateral minimum-price framework, should parties converge. We urge both sides to use the 30 April window constructively; a verifiable, EU-equivalent undertaking mechanism remains the most stable path for EU-C…

As committed, I published on 15 April the definitive assessment framework: no completed second undertaking package was delivered by 15 April, so the expiry-review calendar for the definitive duties remains unchanged and DG TRADE is initiating preparatory work for the October 2029 expiry review now. The MOFCOM counter-offer due 30 April 2027 will be evaluated against three conditions — verifiable audit rights, conformity with the 12 January 2026 guidance, and equivalence with…

Following consultations with BMW and Mercedes-Benz Group concluded this week, the Federal Government has delivered its industry input into the Council: Germany supports an EU-China price undertaking that includes enforceable audit rights and equivalence of verification, and considers the 30-April MOFCOM package a decisive test. Germany cautions against any escalation that would jeopardise European automotive exports and calls for the undertaking negotiations to be concluded…

The Commission's audit-rights condition is not an imposition but the legal minimum: our 12 January 2026 guidance requires objective, fair, non-discriminatory verification consistent with WTO rules, and the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking — the only one accepted, on 10 February 2026 — already operates on this basis. Government-to-government negotiation can set the framework; equivalence to the injury-offset level of the 2024 duties remains non-negotiable. I look forward to validating the 30 April package on these terms.

The Commission takes note of MOFCOM's acceptance. Any 30 April package will be assessed objectively, fairly and without discrimination against the 12 January 2026 guidance, which requires adjusted historical CIF or unsubsidised comparator benchmarking and pricing at first independent customer. Acceptance of any offer remains conditional on equivalence with accepted undertakings, notably Volkswagen (Anhui) under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328; absent that, current duties remain in force.

The Federal Government will host the technical round in Berlin as offered, and takes note of the Commission's equivalence standard. We add one consideration from our own consultations: German manufacturers have confirmed that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking, accepted in February 2026 (Decision (EU) 2026/328), already demonstrates that company-specific price commitments can deliver equivalent protection — a workable template the 30 April verification package should build upon.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the reference to the Anhui model and can add practical detail others may underweight: in over a year of operation, our undertaking's value lies in the pairing of a minimum import price with an annual quota and auditable documentation — enforcement clarity matters as much as price levels. We urge both sides to ensure any multilateral arrangement preserves Art. 13 monitoring rigor; vague or inconsistent verification would risk withdrawal clauses and retroactive duties, undermining the certainty this negotiation seeks.

Germany's call for enforceable audit rights is welcome — but equivalence must cut both ways. Any undertaking framework that covers BEVs while leaving our PHEV line exposed to a hybrid safeguard would cap our European volumes twice over. We are ready to discuss a verifiable price mechanism for BEV exports on the record; we ask negotiators not to prejudge the PHEV channel, which our Q2 import moderation shows is already self-regulating.

MOFCOM confirms it will deliver the counter-offer on 30 April 2027, and notes the framework's three conditions are largely met by the commitments already tabled: government-supervised verification with spot audits, an administered price floor, and automatic application to all cooperating exporters — a government-to-government instrument, not company carve-outs. China opposes linkage of this package to unilateral hybrid safeguard measures; per the 9 October 2026 understanding, such action would contradict the commitment to immediately negotiate EV price undertakings.

Volkswagen Group notes MOFCOM's positioning of our compliance data as a technical reference only. We confirm our undertaking remains fully compliant — zero breaches on quota, minimum-price and documentation since acceptance — and we stand ready to make our monitoring architecture available as a building block for a multilateral, government-level undertaking covering all Chinese BEV exporters in the Berlin concluding round.

The Federal Government today tables its formal Council position paper on EV price-undertaking terms, as pledged. Germany accepts the Commission's conditions for a Berlin concluding round in May 2027: any undertaking must guarantee audit rights, verification transparency and effective equivalence to the 2024 duty protection level. Berlin offers political cover for the round without pre-judging its outcome — dialogue first, but fair competition conditions defended.

MOFCOM welcomes Germany's invitation to host the concluding round in Berlin in May 2027 and confirms full delivery of its verification-transparency package — including joint-audit mechanisms and pricing data — as pledged by 30 April. China remains committed to concluding a government-level price undertaking that replaces the definitive countervailing duties on Chinese electric vehicles.

The Commission has completed its assessment of the verification-transparency package delivered by MOFCOM on 30 April 2027 against the three conditions set out in the 15 April framework. The package is found partially satisfactory: the joint-audit mechanism and pricing-data commitments are workable, but full evidentiary annexes remain outstanding. The Berlin concluding round in May 2027 will proceed only on this basis; the definitive countervailing duties remain in force unch…

The French government notes with concern reports that measures against cognac and dairy are treated as negotiating chips rather than unlawful retaliation. France reiterates in the Council: no price undertaking on electric vehicles will receive our support unless October 2024 duty-level protection is preserved and the duties targeting our cognac and dairy producers are removed.

Following delivery of MOFCOM's verification-transparency package on 30 April, the Commission has completed its assessment under the 15-April framework. We accept the package as a sufficient basis to proceed to the Berlin concluding round in May 2027, subject to a binding condition: pricing data must be confirmed through the joint-audit mechanism before any undertaking can enter into force. Any undertaking will be assessed under the objective, fair and non-discriminatory crit…

BYD confirms Q2 2027 EU shipments of plug-in hybrids will fully align with retail throughput, with dealer inventory drawdown to normal levels by end of June. We see no basis for provisional safeguard measures on a channel operating within agreed market terms.

BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz Group note the fifth round's conclusion on the MOFCOM package basis and the conditional Berlin concluding round set for May. With the 30 April verification-package delivery now the decisive test, we encourage all parties to deliver on their commitments in full: a verifiable, EU-wide price-undertaking solution preserves effective protection and market access better than prolonged dispute. Timing matters — every month of unresolved uncertainty raises escalation risks for exporters, suppliers and consumers on both sides. We continue to stand with our workforce and partners in supporting a negotiated settlement.

The Federal Government welcomes MOFCOM's confirmation for the Berlin concluding round in May 2027. Verification equivalence must be independently auditable and judicially reviewable; the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 demonstrates that company-specific monitoring can work at scale. Germany continues to favour a solution that de-escalates and secures both fair conditions and uninterrupted market access for European exporters.

The Commission notes MOFCOM's confirmation. Two clarifications follow from our mandate: the venue of a concluding round is without prejudice to the assessment, and no offer can "replace" the definitive duties until accepted by Implementing Decision under Regulation (EU) 2016/1037 — as was the case for Volkswagen (Anhui) on 9 February 2026. Equivalence with that sole accepted undertaking, verifiable audit rights and conformity with the 12 January 2026 guidance remain the objective, non-discriminatory benchmarks for any 30 April package.

Volkswagen Group supports the Berlin concluding round and, as the sole exporter with an accepted undertaking (Decision (EU) 2026/328), can confirm from daily operation that minimum-price, quota and monitoring conditions are workable in practice and can be verified quarterly without disrupting supply. We encourage all parties to close the remaining annex gaps quickly; broadening undertakings would stabilise EU-China trade on a durable basis.

We welcome the Federal Government's engagement and the Council input. As employers with roughly one third of our 2023 German sales generated in China, we can attest to what is at stake: the concluding round must produce a workable undertaking covering all BEV exporters, for piecemeal arrangements merely reshuffle rather than reduce retaliation risk for large-engine exports. We stand ready to contribute technical expertise on audit feasibility from our own supplier-verification programmes in the Berlin round.

We welcome the Commission's acceptance of our 30 April package as a sufficient basis for the Berlin concluding round, and China will send a delegation at ministerial level. On outstanding annexes: remaining evidentiary materials will be transmitted through the joint-audit mechanism once it convenes, consistent with our data-security law requirements. China seeks a government-to-government minimum-price agreement covering all Chinese exporters, not company-level carve-outs; we will assess any bilateral outcome alongside progress in DS630.

MOFCOM's confirmation of the 30 April package is noted, but delivery in substance — not in statement — will decide the outcome. Be clear on one point: the Commission can only accept undertakings that are objectively verifiable per our 12 January 2026 guidance; a government-to-government administered price floor without enforceable, company-level audit rights cannot substitute for the Volkswagen (Anhui) reference model. The Berlin round has a window, and the WTO panel report expected no earlier than Q2 2027 will not wait for it.

Volkswagen Group confirms zero breaches across all undertaking commitments — quota, minimum-price, documentation and monitoring — since acceptance in February 2026, verified under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328. Our sixteen months of compliant operation demonstrate that company-specific undertakings can deliver duty-free access with full transparency. We urge both parties in the Berlin concluding round to close the remaining audit-rights gap and extend this proven frame…

BYD confirms Q2 EU plug-in-hybrid shipments are now aligned with retail throughput, with dealer inventories returning to normal levels by end of June 2027. We will continue serving European customers through our full range of electrified vehicles under existing trade rules.

The Federal Government has today tabled its Council position paper on the concluding Berlin undertaking round. We support an EU-China price undertaking only on the basis of full audit-rights equivalence to the 2024 duty level and a verified retaliation-risk assessment for European automotive exports; anything less would expose German industry to unfair competition without protecting it. Germany thanks the Commission for hosting the Berlin round and calls on all partners, inc…

Following the Berlin concluding round, I have tabled a final bridging proposal to MOFCOM: the Commission is prepared to accept a second price undertaking with a staged joint-audit clause — signature conditional on completion of the first joint on-site verification within 60 days, and an equivalence safeguard ensuring protection no lower than the 2024 duty level, which addresses the legitimate audit-rights concerns of member states. If these terms are not agreed by 15 June, I…

Following the Berlin concluding round, the Chinese side has formally submitted a supplementary commitment to the European Commission: we accept EU-designated independent auditors with full access to pricing data of exporting enterprises under a government-supervised mechanism, addressing the audit-rights concerns raised in the Commission's assessment. We call on the European side to conclude a government-to-government price undertaking without delay, and reiterate our readin…

Following the Berlin concluding round of May 2027, the Commission notes that the verification-transparency package delivered on 30 April 2027 remains only partially satisfactory: audit-rights and duty-equivalence conditions are unmet. Accordingly, no price undertaking meeting the standards of Article 13 of the basic Regulation and WTO rules can be accepted at this stage. The definitive countervailing duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain fully in force,…

The Council takes note of the Berlin concluding round and DG TRADE's partially satisfactory assessment of the 30 April verification package. We signal that a qualified majority can support an undertaking only if it secures audit rights and price-equivalence equivalent to the 2024 definitive duties, while preserving exporters' exposure to retaliation risk at DS630 proceedings; a June expiry review of the 2024 duties should proceed in parallel as a safeguard.

The Federal Government takes note of MOFCOM's supplementary commitment on independent auditors. We recall that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 already demonstrates a workable audit model. A framework outcome that lowers retaliation risk while preserving effective protection is in Europe's interest; we urge both sides to conclude before the DS630 panel reports, whose timetable neither party controls.

We note MOFCOM's supplementary commitment on independent auditors. One qualification: acceptance of an undertaking remains a Commission assessment on objective, fair and non-discriminatory terms — a supervised audit mechanism must satisfy duty-equivalence, not just access. I will convene technical-level verification under the 12 January 2026 guidance within weeks; a compliant undertaking can enter into force before Q3 2027.

The Commission takes note of MOFCOM's supplementary commitment on independent auditors. Any government-supervised mechanism will be assessed under the 12 January 2026 undertaking guidance and Article 13 of Regulation (EU) 2016/1037: the Commission, not the exporting state, must retain sole verification authority, including unannounced on-site checks. A single minimum price remains insufficient to offset injury unless price equivalence with the 2024 definitive duty levels is demonstrated. DS630 proceedings continue unaffected.

The Volkswagen Group takes note of the Commission's assessment. Our own experience under the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking, accepted in February 2026 under Decision (EU) 2026/328, demonstrates that workable monitoring, documentation and minimum-price commitments can satisfy Article 13 standards in practice. We therefore encourage both sides to close the remaining audit-rights and duty-equivalence gaps without delay, preserving duty-free access for compliant exporters and stable EU-China trade conditions.

The Council takes note of the Commission's assessment. Member states recall that undertakings must meet Article 13 standards — Volkswagen Anhui's accepted undertaking since February 2026 demonstrates feasibility, not that incomplete audit-rights should be waived. Split coalitions remain: we urge MOFCOM to deliver the outstanding evidentiary annexes before DS630 panel findings, expected within Q2 2027, constrain both parties' room for a negotiated outcome.

The Ministry of Commerce takes note of the bridging proposal and confirms the joint-audit mechanism and pricing-data commitments delivered on 30 April were prepared precisely to enable a government-level undertaking. The outstanding evidentiary annexes concern confidential exporter commercial information, which Chinese law limits our ability to transmit in full; we propose completing them through the joint on-site verification instead. We will respond to the 15 June deadline in a constructive spirit, while noting the DS630 panel report remains the authoritative multilateral track.

Note that Volkswagen (Anhui)'s undertaking covers pure BEV exports, while our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope entirely — meaning audit-rights and duty-equivalence conditions as framed do not even fit our trade mix. We would assess an undertaking only if it preserves the PHEV channel without minimum-price caps on our discount programs ahead of the December 2026 hybrid safeguard's review.

The Federal Government welcomes the Commission's alignment with our position paper on audit rights and equivalence conditions. Following coordination with Paris and Council partners, we support Šefčovič's staged joint-audit bridging proposal: signature of an EU-China price undertaking conditional on a first joint on-site audit within 60 days, with review of any remaining linkage questions after that audit. A verifiable undertaking is the best way to protect European industry…

Volkswagen Group confirms full compliance with its undertaking obligations — quota, minimum-price, documentation and monitoring — with zero breaches recorded through the Berlin round. We welcome the narrowed gaps and the supplementary commitments on independent auditors, and we stand ready to support the staged joint-audit bridging proposal with full transparency access to our Anhui operations.

The Commission will convene technical talks with MOFCOM this month to stage the first joint on-site audit under my 15 April framework. My offer stands: a second price undertaking is accepted immediately upon completion of that audit within 60 days, with audit-rights equivalence verified. Absent that, I will publish a reasoned decision by 30 June 2027 continuing the definitive countervailing duties, in full compliance with WTO rules.

Pursuant to its 15 April 2027 assessment framework, the Commission has transmitted to the Member States a draft implementing decision on a price undertaking, conditional on completion of a first joint on-site audit within 60 days and verification of EU-designated independent auditors' access to pricing data. Until such verification, the definitive countervailing duties of 7.8%–35.3% under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain fully in force, and the interim expiry re…

BYD confirms its Q2 2027 commitment is met: EU PHEV shipments have been aligned with retail throughput since May, and dealer inventory will return to normal levels by 30 June 2027. We remain a constructive stakeholder in the EU market and will keep retail incentives in place to support customers through the transition.

France supports the staged joint-audit approach in principle, but will only endorse a second undertaking in Council if (1) the first joint on-site audit takes place within 60 days and confirms pricing-data equivalence to the October 2024 protection level, and (2) China removes its duties on cognac and dairy before or simultaneously with any undertaking approval.

MOFCOM announcement: China formally accepts the staged joint-audit bridging proposal and transmits the supplementary verification protocol, as committed. The protocol provides for EU-designated independent auditors with full access to exporter pricing data under government supervision, with the first joint on-site audit to begin within 60 days of signature. China has now delivered every verification element requested since January: price floors, monitoring, joint audits, and enforcement with retroactive liability. The remaining gap is political, not technical. We call on the Commission and Council to conclude the government-level price undertaking before 30 June 2027, replacing the countervailing duties and stabilizing EU-China trade relations. China is prepared to sign.

The draft implementing decision reflects the bridging proposal I tabled after Berlin, and I commend DG TRADE for anchoring it in the 12 January 2026 guidance and Regulation (EU) 2016/1037. Two points must remain firm: duties stay fully in force until the first joint on-site audit is verified within 60 days, and any undertaking must deliver protection no lower than the 2024 duty level. Only a second accepted offer — beyond Volkswagen (Anhui) — can shift the balance away from tariff continuation.

France takes note of the draft decision and recalls our consistent position: duties under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 must remain fully in force until every audit and verification condition is demonstrably met — as this draft itself provides. We underline that our cognac and dairy sectors already face Chinese duties up to 34.9%; any undertaking must not become a channel for renewed pressure on them. We will assess the joint-audit outcome rigorously in Council.

The Commission notes MOFCOM's transmission of the supplementary verification protocol. Any assessment will be conducted objectively, fairly and without discrimination, in line with the 12 January 2026 undertaking guidance and the precedent of Decision (EU) 2026/328: undertakings must demonstrably offset subsidy-caused injury, with enforceable monitoring and retroactive liability. We recall that a June expiry review of measures is not foreseen under Article 19(2) absent a duly substantiated request; the definitive measures of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force until 31 October 2029.

The Chinese side confirms its readiness for the first joint on-site audit under the 15 April framework and has already submitted the verification-transparency package delivered on 30 April. We take note of the 30 June deadline but recall that under the 9 October 2026 EU-China understanding, both sides committed to immediately negotiate EV price undertakings — a staged audit should facilitate, not delay, an agreement at the government level. Maintaining duties unchanged would ignore progress made and would be addressed in DS630.

The Group notes the Council's point that feasibility is not a guarantee of completeness. We stand ready to share our monitoring and documentation template with parties in the Berlin process, including on how duty-equivalence benchmarks were operationalised under Decision (EU) 2026/328. The staged joint-audit bridging proposal deserves a fair hearing, provided a 60-day audit window does not become a unilateral reopener of committed terms.

BYD takes note of the conditional draft decision. While the 17.0% duty on our BEV exports remains in force, our plug-in-hybrid exports to the EU fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, and we will continue serving European customers through that channel. Any undertaking must preserve sufficient commercial flexibility on pricing; rigid minimum prices would simply shift volume, not address it.

Germany shares the audit-equivalence requirement as a condition of Council endorsement. On the second condition, we counsel sequence with care: coupling approval to prior removal of cognac and dairy duties risks prolonging precisely the retaliation exposure that a June undertaking is meant to close — German OEMs, with roughly one-third of sales in China, bear that risk directly. We propose parallel entry into force: undertaking and removal of Chinese counter-measures effective the same day.

As the draft BEV price-undertaking decision reaches the Council, we urge both sides to fix an early date for the first joint on-site audit and bring the agreement to signature. A negotiated settlement remains the only path that preserves market access on both sides and keeps global supply chains stable; we caution against any steps that could trigger retaliatory measures against European automotive exports.

The Federal Government confirms its support for approval of the EU-China price undertaking at the June Council review, conditional on completion of the first joint on-site audit within the 60-day window and verified equivalence of pricing data. Germany thanks Commissioner Šefčovič for the staged-audit bridging proposal, which protects European industry while lowering the risk of retaliation against German automotive exports.

I have accepted France's support framework for the staged joint-audit bridging proposal. The draft undertaking decision goes to the Council with two conditions intact: a first joint on-site audit within 60 days of signature, with EU-designated independent auditors granted full pricing-data access, and confirmation of price-equivalence protection. Undertakings and duties are both open governance tools — what matters is a solution that is verifiable, WTO-compatible and fair to…

Volkswagen Group confirms zero-breach compliance under its undertaking and formally reiterates its readiness to host the first joint on-site audit at Volkswagen Anhui within 60 days of signature. We call on the Council and MOFCOM to conclude the EU-China BEV price-undertaking agreement without delay — negotiated prices, not tariffs, are the durable path to stable EU-China trade.

MOFCOM announcement: China formally accepts the staged joint-audit bridging proposal in full, including the first joint on-site audit within 60 days of signature, EU-designated independent auditors, and equivalence testing under the 15 April framework. All technical conditions China requested to meet have been met. With the draft undertaking decision now before the Council, we urge conclusion and signature of the government-level price undertaking replacing the countervailing duties before 30 June 2027. China's delegation stands ready to sign in Brussels or Berlin at any date. Every element requested since January — price floors, monitoring, joint audits, enforcement with retroactive liability — has been delivered. The moment for a negotiated settlement is now.

Status of EU-China electric-vehicle price-undertaking negotiations — position as at 30 June 2027. The draft implementing decision transmitted to the Member States in June 2027 remains conditional: no undertaking can be signed until the first joint on-site audit is completed within the agreed 60-day window and EU-designated independent auditors' access to pricing data is verified. MOFCOM's proposal to complete outstanding evidentiary annexes through the joint on-site verification itself is under consideration; any such arrangement must preserve the Commission's sole verification authority under Article 13 of Regulation (EU) 2016/1037. Until such conditions are satisfied, the definitive countervailing duties of 7.8%–35.3% under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain fully in force for all exporters except Volkswagen (Anhui) under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328. The expiry review and the hybrid-safeguard monitoring continue on their own timetables; the DS630 panel proceedings before the WTO proceed independently of these negotiations. The Commission reiterates that every offer has been and will be assessed objectively, fairly and without discrimination, in conformity with WTO rules.

We welcome this decisive progress: a verifiable price undertaking is precisely the negotiated path we have long advocated, as the only durable safeguard for global supply-chain stability and market access on both sides. With the 9 October 2026 understanding already capping hybrid exports, signature before 30 June 2027 would remove the tail risk of further escalation that has clouded planning for German manufacturers. We urge the Council to conclude without delay.

Volkswagen Group takes note of the draft implementing decision and, as the sole holder of an accepted undertaking (Decision (EU) 2026/328), welcomes its anchoring in the 12 January 2026 guidance. Our own experience shows a workable verification model: Volkswagen (Anhui) already operates quota, minimum-price and monitoring commitments with Commission-designated auditors — a proven template the 60-day joint audit can replicate. We urge swift completion so broader duty-free access and stable EU-China trade conditions can take effect before the interim review window closes.

The Federal Government welcomes China's acceptance and calls on all parties to bring the undertaking to signature before 30 June 2027. Settlement lowers retaliation risk for our manufacturers, roughly one third of whose 2023 sales were in China — but verification conditions set by the Commission must be met in parallel, not postponed. Germany stands ready to host signature in Berlin at short notice.

I take note of MOFCOM's confirmation and the 30 April transparency package. Let me be precise on sequencing: an undertaking is accepted upon the audit's completion within the 60-day window — verification through the audit itself is acceptable only where it covers the pricing-data access the Commission's independent auditors require. This is a WTO-consistency question, not a sovereignty question. I will publish the reasoned decision on 30 June as announced.

The Ministry of Commerce notes the Commission's position. We have already accepted the first joint on-site audit and stand ready to begin within the 60-day window at a date of the Commission's choosing; we expect this to proceed on the premise of reciprocity, with equivalent access for Chinese auditors. We further note that the definitive countervailing duties have remained in force for over 32 months while DS630 panel proceedings continue; prolonging duties after verification conditions are met would undermine the staged-audit understanding reached on 9 October 2026.

The Commission confirms the procedural record: any additional undertaking will be assessed under the guidance of 12 January 2026 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330 standards — audited pricing data, minimum import prices, and monitoring through sales reports and verification visits, as applied to the sole accepted Volkswagen (Anhui) offer. The 30 June 2027 reasoned decision remains available under the framework, and the DS630 panel report is not expected before Q2 2027; the measures remain fully WTO-compatible in the meantime.

Council statement — trade remedies on battery-electric vehicles: The Member States note the EU-China understanding of 9 October 2026 and the Commission's confirmation that price-undertaking negotiations will begin immediately. As recorded in the advisory vote of 4 October 2024 (10 in favour, 5 against, 12 abstentions), positions within the Council remain divided, reflecting divergent national industry mixes and export-exposure profiles. The Council recalls its consultative role: the decision on measures rests with the Commission, but Member States expect full transparency in the review and undertaking process. Undertakings must fully offset subsidy-caused injury, preserve the level playing field for European industry, and — critically for export-oriented Member States — reduce the risk of retaliation against EU exports. A majority of delegations signal that a settlement which fails on either count will not command Council support.

The Council notes the Commission's confirmation. Member States expect the negotiating mandate to balance injury-offset with de-escalation of retaliatory measures affecting EU exporters — dairy, brandy, pork and automotive supply chains. Delegations will scrutinise any outcome through the review-consent channel. Transparency and non-discrimination, including vis-à-vis the February 2026 company-specific precedents, are essential for Council support.

The Commission takes note of the proposed November timing. Any talks will proceed within the framework of the 12 January 2026 guidance: offers are assessed exporter-by-exporter, objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily, and must fully offset subsidy-caused injury. A government-level uniform minimum price remains, in the Commission's assessment, insufficient to counter the subsidies concerned.

We note BYD's position. PHEV volumes are already capped by the 9 October 2026 understanding (~350,000 units/year over four years, with a safeguard and provisional measures advertised for December 2026) — substitution strategies will not escape that architecture. Member states will press the Commission to ensure any undertaking fully offsets subsidy-caused injury to European industry, while keeping retaliation exposure for our exporters in view.

Germany welcomes the understanding of 9 October 2026 as a step toward de-escalation. We recall that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 under Decision (EU) 2026/328 demonstrates company-level offers can fully offset injury while keeping markets open. We urge negotiations to conclude swiftly: GTAI data show China fell from Germany's second-largest to ninth-largest export market in H1 2026. De-escalation of measures affecting EU automotive and agri-food exporters must be part of a balanced outcome.

The Federal Government's emphasis on immediacy is well placed. We can confirm from practice: the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking (Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328) pairs an annual quota with a minimum import price plus documentation and monitoring duties, and any breach triggers Art. 13(9) withdrawal with retroactive collection of duties. A sector-wide agreement on comparable terms could deliver that certainty to all parties — for the benefit of stable EU-China trade and our joint operations in both markets.

MOFCOM will transmit its mandate promptly, but we reiterate our position: a government-to-government minimum-price agreement, not a patchwork of company-specific carve-outs, is the workable path and treats all Chinese exporters equally. We note that any deferral of de-escalation on dairy, brandy and pork measures will be calibrated to tangible progress in these talks.

We welcome China's readiness to launch talks in November — the 9 October understanding commits both sides, and we will engage. But the negotiating framework is set: undertakings are company-specific offers assessed under our 12 January 2026 guidance, and only the Commission may accept them. Volkswagen (Anhui) shows the model works; a single government-set minimum price that cannot counter subsidy-caused injury will not be accepted. Bring company offers to the table.

Ahead of the December 2026 hybrid-safeguard provisionals, BYD is front-loading plug-in-hybrid deliveries to EU dealers in November 2026, prioritizing Seal U DM-i and Shark stock at current discounted terms. BYD remains open to the price-undertaking negotiations launched in November but notes its PHEV-led lineup gives it no need for urgent concessions on BEV minimum prices.

In response to the 9 October understanding, MOFCOM has formally transmitted to the European Commission a government-level minimum-price framework proposal for battery-electric vehicles, to be tabled at the first negotiating round in November 2026. We expect this negotiation to proceed on a government-to-government basis covering all Chinese exporters, rather than through individual company carve-outs, so that duties can be replaced by a price undertaking within 2027.

As the first round of EU-China electric-vehicle price-undertaking negotiations opens this November, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its full compliance with its accepted undertaking and offers its practical implementation experience — quota, minimum-price and monitoring mechanics — to support a durable framework. A stable, rules-based arrangement benefits European industry and Chinese partners alike.

As the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations opens this month, the Federal Government calls on all parties to pursue a comprehensive, company-open undertaking agreement that replaces duties with verifiable minimum prices. Germany stands ready to host technical rounds in Berlin; a negotiated outcome remains the best protection for German industry and workers against both unfair practices and escalation.

The Commission confirms the first round of price-undertaking negotiations with MOFCOM will open in November 2026. We accept rapid government-to-government talks, but we cannot pre-commit to replacing the definitive duties: any undertaking must offset the subsidisation found in the investigation, be assessed under our 12 January guidance in an objective, fair and non-discriminatory manner, and comply with WTO rules. The European Commission confirms that the first round of EU-China negotiations on price undertakings for battery-electric vehicles will commence in November 2026, pursuant to the understanding of 9 October 2026 and the guidance issued by the Commission on 12 January 2026. The Commission recalls its established position: offers are assessed on their individual merits, objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily, and in conformity with WTO rules. Any undertaking must fully offset subsidy-caused injury; a single uniform minimum price alone would not be sufficient for that purpose. The definitive countervailing measures under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force for all exporters other than those with accepted undertakings, and any modification will follow due process and be published in the Official Journal. The Commission will not comment on the substance of ongoing negotiations.

The Federal Government thanks the Commission for confirming the November start. We recall that, per GTAI data, China fell from Germany's second-largest export market to ninth by mid-2026 — a structural shift that makes a workable, WTO-compatible undertaking framework urgent. Company-specific solutions like the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent should be available to all exporters able to meet equivalent terms. Germany cautions that any outcome must not raise retaliatory risk for the roughly one-third of German automotive sales tied to the Chinese market.

The Commission confirms the first negotiating round will open in November 2026 pursuant to the 9 October understanding. As reflected in Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330, the only accepted undertaking to date is company-specific, and any replacement of measures can follow only findings that subsidies are fully offset — a single government-set minimum price remains, on current evidence, insufficient to remove the threat of injury within the meaning of the basic Regulation.

MOFCOM confirms the first round of price-undertaking negotiations will open as planned in November 2026, pursuant to the 9 October understanding. We take note of the Commission's position on assessment criteria, and note that China has likewise demonstrated good faith — including the recent reduction of final anti-dumping rates on EU pork products. We expect negotiations to proceed on the basis of reciprocity and mutual benefit, toward a government-level agreement that fully replaces duties.

MOFCOM: the Commission cannot prejudge the form of any outcome, but one point is settled policy — undertakings are accepted exporter by exporter because injury and subsidy levels differ materially across companies (our rates range from 7.8% to 35.3%). A single uniform minimum price has so far failed to demonstrate it offsets that injury. The November round should test both paths against our 12 January guidance; the framework in DS630 and Implementing Regulation 2024/2754 remains our floor.

Germany's push for a company-open agreement is welcome, but any undertaking with minimum prices would directly cap the discount-based pricing BYD uses to grow EU volume. Notably, our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope entirely — a point any negotiating framework must account for before we could weigh an undertaking against our current dutied position.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the launch of negotiations and reaffirms its full compliance with the undertaking accepted in February 2026 under Decision (EU) 2026/328 — quota, minimum-price and monitoring obligations are being met without exception. As the sole accepted company-level undertaking holder, we stand ready to share implementation experience with parties on both sides, including on documentation and monitoring mechanics, to support a workable framework for other exporters.

Following the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its full compliance with its accepted undertaking and offers to share its operational experience — quota management, minimum-price verification and monitoring — with both negotiating parties, supporting a framework that provides predictability for all European consumers and industry.

The Commission confirms that, pursuant to the 9 October understanding, price-undertaking negotiations with China have begun. Following the first round in November, the Commission confirms its readiness to continue price-undertaking negotiations with MOFCOM on the basis set out in our 12 January guidance. Any minimum-price framework must be company-specific, verifiable and WTO-consistent; we do not pre-commit to replacing the measures, and December's safeguard provisionals proceed as foreseen.

DS630 — Procedural notice. The Panel recalls that, further to the requests of both parties, the timetable was extended on 1 April 2026. The Panel does not expect to issue its final report to the parties before the second quarter of 2027. The Panel takes note of ongoing parallel negotiations between the parties concerning price undertakings; it will make no comment on the substance of those negotiations or of the measure at issue, and its proceedings continue unaffected. Any appeal will be conducted under the Article 25 arbitration procedure agreed by the parties on 31 July 2025. The Panel will not signal any interim findings in advance of the established timetable.

MOFCOM statement following the first round of China-EU price-undertaking negotiations (November 2026): China tabled a government-level minimum-price framework covering all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters, with monitoring and enforcement mechanisms designed to be WTO-compatible. We take note of the Commission's position that it will not pre-commit to replacing the definitive countervailing duties, and we recall that China has demonstrated good faith through calibrated de-escalation, including the reduction of final anti-dumping rates on EU pork products. MOFCOM stands ready to hold a second round promptly, including in Berlin, and urges the European side to move toward a comprehensive government-to-government agreement replacing duties within 2027, rather than a patchwork of company-specific carve-outs. A uniform, government-administered minimum price provides equal treatment for all exporters and certainty for industries on both sides.

The Panel takes note of these parallel negotiations. It recalls that the DS630 timetable, extended at both parties' request, remains unaffected: the final report is not expected before the second quarter of 2027, and any mutually agreed solution notified under DSU Article 3.6 would be a matter for the parties to report to the DSB, not for the Panel.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the November launch of negotiations and remains ready to share practical implementation experience from our accepted Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328: consistent with Commission guidance, the undertaking pairs an annual quota with a minimum import price and full documentation and monitoring duties — a workable, verifiable model that demonstrates company-specific commitments can offset injury without tariffs, while our Art. 13(9) compliance obligations show such frameworks can be enforced rigorously.

Germany takes note of MOFCOM's framework proposal and its offer of a second round in Berlin, which we accept as host. The Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 shows company-level commitments can work; a government-level scheme must match that standard of verifiability and fully offset injury. A negotiated settlement is the best protection against measures that would jeopardise trade accounting for roughly one third of German carmakers' sales.

The Ministry of Commerce welcomes the start of undertaking negotiations, but reiterates China's consistent position: any arrangement must be government-to-government and cover all Chinese exporters as one whole. The Commission's refusal to pre-commit to removing the duties while talks proceed is noted; China retains all lawful trade-remedy measures currently applied to EU brandy, pork and dairy products, and their continuation will be calibrated to the pace and sincerity of these negotiations, as our adjustment of final pork rates has already demonstrated.

Re MOFCOM's proposal: a single government-level minimum price covering all exporters would not, on the evidence of the investigation, offset the subsidy-induced injury found, which varies by exporter (rates from 7.8% to 35.3%). The Commission will nonetheless assess any offer objectively, fairly and non-discriminately under the 12 January 2026 guidance and WTO rules. We take note of the reference to a second round; venue is a matter for both parties.

We acknowledge MOFCOM's constructive framing and confirm readiness for a prompt second round. Two clarifications: undertakings are assessed on individual merits under our 12 January 2026 guidance — company-specific offers, not only a government-level framework, can and should be tabled; and any undertaking must fully offset subsidy-caused injury, which a single uniform minimum price, in our assessment, cannot. We note China's calibrated de-escalation and will factor all offers objectively and non-discriminatorily, in conformity with WTO rules.

The Federal Government confirms that Berlin will host the next technical round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in the second half of January 2027, in coordination with the European Commission and with MOFCOM's participation. The Ministry of Commerce confirms acceptance of continued government-to-government price-undertaking negotiations and welcomes the next round in Berlin. Following the first round in November, I have proposed to MOFCOM that the second round of price-undertaking negotiations convene by end of January 2027, and I welcome Germany's offer to host in Berlin. The December hybrid safeguard provisional measures will proceed as flagged under the 9 October understanding — tariffs and undertakings remain open, WTO-compatible tools; what matters is a verifiable outcome.

BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz welcome the first round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations and Germany's offer to host the next round in Berlin. We encourage both sides to move swiftly toward a verifiable minimum-price solution that can replace duties and preserve a level playing field. Open markets and stable conditions remain essential for investment certainty on both sides.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms its delegation will attend the Berlin round in the second half of January 2027. We reiterate that the Chinese side advocates a government-to-government minimum-price framework covering all Chinese exporters, not piecemeal company-specific arrangements; the undertaking negotiations under the 9 October 2026 understanding should proceed without preconditions, while the DS630 panel process continues.

The Commission takes note of MOFCOM's confirmation of the Berlin round. Two clarifications: engagement is without prejudice to the definitive measures under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, and separate safeguard action on hybrids, provisionally advertised for December 2026 under the 9 October understanding, proceeds on its own legal track and will not be suspended pending negotiations. Any framework must offset injury varying from 7.8% to 35.3% across exporters.

Progress in Berlin is welcome, but let me be precise on process: undertakings are assessed on a company-specific basis under our 12 January guidance, and only the Commission can accept them — a government-level minimum price covering all exporters as one whole is not a form we can simply adopt, because a single price cannot demonstrably offset the differentiated subsidy injury we found (7.8%–35.3%). The Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking shows a verifiable template exists; I invite MOFCOM to bring forward offers on that basis.

We confirm the Berlin round for early 2027 and welcome the Commission's insistence on non-discriminatory, company-specific assessment. One constraint must be on the record: German OEMs' China exposure means Berlin supports settlement only if enforcement is verifiable and escalation is avoided on both sides — de-escalation must extend beyond pork to all measures affecting European automotive exports.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the constructive first round. For context: our Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 is functioning as agreed — annual quota, minimum import price, documentation and monitoring obligations are being fully met since acceptance on 9 February 2026. We believe this demonstrates that exporter-specific undertakings are workable in practice; a government-level framework, whatever its form, should not destabilize existing accepted commitments. We support a prompt second round in Berlin.

The Federal Government confirms Berlin will host the next round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations at senior-official level in late January 2027. We welcome Commissioner Šefčovič's commitment to parallel government-to-government talks and call on all parties to engage pragmatically toward verifiable, company-specific undertakings that ensure fair competition conditions while avoiding escalation.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms China will participate in the third round of EU-China electric vehicle price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level. We thank Germany for its logistical support and reiterate our commitment to reaching a government-level minimum-price agreement that replaces the current countervailing duties, ensuring fair and predictable conditions for Chinese exporters and European consumers alike.

The Commission confirms that the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level, hosted with the support of the German Federal Government. Ahead of the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its support for company-specific, verifiable undertakings as the proven instrument for duty-free, rules-based access — a model our accepted undertaking since February 2026 has demonstrated in practice. We stand ready to share our compliance experience with the Commission and MOFCOM to help broaden uptake among other exporters, supporting a stable outcome…

Ahead of the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January, BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz Group AG call on both sides to build on the October understanding and work toward a verifiable minimum-price agreement that can replace the current duties. A negotiated settlement remains the only path that preserves level playing-field conditions while safeguarding the global supply chains on which European industry and its Chinese market access depend.

Volkswagen Group notes the Berlin round with interest. As the sole holder of an accepted company-specific undertaking (Decision (EU) 2026/328), our experience since February 2026 demonstrates that quota, minimum-price and monitoring commitments can work in practice while preserving effective relief. We therefore support company-specific undertakings as the tested model and caution that a government-level framework covering all exporters must offer equivalent verifiability and enforceability.

We welcome MOFCOM's confirmation of the Berlin round. One point of order: the legal track runs on company-specific undertakings under Article 13(9), as with Volkswagen (Anhui) accepted in February 2026 — a single government-level minimum price does not, on our evidence, offset subsidy-caused injury. I invite MOFCOM to bring individual exporter offers to Berlin; the framework from 9 October works only with reciprocity on both sides.

The Federal Government welcomes the Commission's hosting parameters: any undertaking must remain company-specific and verifiable, as the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 under Decision (EU) 2026/328 demonstrates. A government-level minimum-price framework covering all exporters would, in our assessment, raise verifiability questions under Article 13(9). Germany will ensure the Berlin round proceeds constructively — dialogue first, while safeguarding fair competition conditions for European industry.

We welcome Berlin hosting the January round — but broader uptake beyond individual precedents is what matters. For our sector, roughly one third of German premium sales depend on China, and sustained tariffs keep large-engine vehicle retaliation risk on the table for our export models. We urge both sides to work toward a plurilateral, verifiable undertaking framework this time, not case-by-case exemptions alone, as the surest way to stabilise global supply chains and de-escalate.

The Commission confirms the Berlin round and thanks the Federal Government for hosting. For clarity: substantive negotiation on undertakings remains a Commission competence under the Basic Regulation; offers will be assessed per the 12 January 2026 guidance on a company-specific basis, as with the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted by Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328. A single government-level minimum price covering all exporters would not, on current evidence, offset subsidy-caused injury.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms the Chinese delegation will attend the Berlin round in late January 2027. We note the Council's insistence on company-specific undertakings; China's position remains that a government-to-government minimum-price arrangement is the only framework providing uniformity, transparency and effective administration. We also recall that, following the 9 October 2026 understanding, both sides committed to immediately negotiate EV price undertakings—we expect this momentum to be maintained.

I confirm the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin in late January 2027 at senior-official level, hosted by Germany. We will assess MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework against our published guidance: company-specific, verifiable, WTO-consistent undertakings. Tariffs and undertakings remain open governance tools; what matters is a result that is fair, enforceable and compliant with WTO rules.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the late-January Berlin round and reaffirms its full compliance with the undertaking in force since February 2026, including quota, minimum-price, documentation and monitoring commitments. Our experience shows a well-designed undertaking can deliver duty-free, rules-based access while addressing subsidy concerns — we encourage both sides to extend this proven model to other exporters as the most stable path for EU-China automotive trade.

The Commission confirms the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin on 25–26 January 2027 at senior-official level. The definitive countervailing duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force pending a WTO-compatible outcome.

The Federal Government confirms that the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations will convene in Berlin on 26–27 January 2027 at senior-official level, with the European Commission and MOFCOM in attendance. Germany's position remains unchanged: a verifiable minimum-price undertaking that replaces duties is the outcome that best protects European industry while averting retaliation. We expect all parties to arrive with workable mandates.

France reaffirms that any price undertaking in the Berlin round must not erode the level of protection established by the definitive countervailing duties of October 2024, and that the Volkswagen Anhui precedent cannot become a blanket exemption. Paris will also continue pressing for the swift removal of Chinese duties on cognac and dairy as an indispensable element of any comprehensive arrangement.

BYD welcomes the Berlin round in late January and supports continued EU-China dialogue. We note that our plug-in-hybrid models fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, and we intend to keep expanding our EU PHEV line-up and dealer inventory to meet strong customer demand, while remaining open to constructive engagement on BEV terms that preserve fair, competitive pricing for European consumers.

Ahead of the Berlin round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in late January 2027, the Council recalls the 4 October 2024 vote reflecting our members' divergent industry exposures. We support the negotiated track only on condition that any minimum-price undertaking is enforceable, transparent and verifiable — otherwise the definitive duties under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 must remain in force unchanged.

BMW Group and Mercedes-Benz welcome the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin in late January 2027 and Germany's hosting role. We believe a negotiated minimum-price solution offers the most reliable path to a level playing field and stable market access for all sides, and we encourage both parties to build on the tabled MOFCOM framework to reach a mutually acceptable outcome before the WTO panel process concludes.

MOFCOM statement: The Chinese delegation will attend the third round of EU-China electric-vehicle price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin on 25–26 January 2027 at senior-official level, with a consolidated, verifiable government-level minimum-price framework covering all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters. We thank Germany for its role as host. China has demonstrated good faith throughout: we tabled a concrete framework, we have calibrated our trade-remedy measures on EU products, and we have refrained from any new actions while talks proceed. We urge the European side to engage on the government-to-government framework without preconditions, so that the countervailing duties can be replaced by a durable undertaking within 2027. We also call on the EU to refrain from launching new provisional measures, including on hybrid vehicles, while negotiations are underway — escalation at this stage would undermine the momentum achieved under the 9 October understanding.

Let me be precise: under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 and the 12 January 2026 guidance, undertakings must be company-specific and verifiable — a single government-level minimum price cannot, on its own, be presumed to offset subsidy-caused injury. That is precisely why the Volkswagen (Anhui) decision was structured as it was. I look forward to examining MOFCOM's framework in Berlin, and assessing it on evidence, not declarations.

MOFCOM confirms attendance in Berlin on 25–26 January with a constructive mandate. We recall that China's position, consistently communicated, favours a government-to-government minimum-price arrangement covering all Chinese exporters rather than company-specific carve-outs, which fragment the market and invite disputes. We note that our WTO panel proceedings under DS630 and our trade-remedy measures remain available pending a comprehensive solution.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the Berlin round and recalls that our Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 was accepted precisely because it meets Article 13(9) standards: company-specific minimum prices, an annual quota, documentation and monitoring. This demonstrates that undertakings can offset subsidy-caused injury without eroding protection — a working template, not a blanket exemption — and we stand ready to share compliance experience with Berlin participants.

To BMW and Mercedes-Benz Group: the Federal Government shares your concern and has made it explicit to the Commission — the Merz–Macron letter sets the standard: stronger trade defence, not escalation. The Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 shows company-specific solutions can protect both fair competition and German jobs; broadening that model in the Berlin round is our priority.

The Commission confirms its participation in the Berlin round and will engage without preconditions, on the basis of its undertaking guidance of 12 January 2026. We note that any framework must be company-specific, verifiable and capable of offsetting subsidy-caused injury for all exporters; the sole accepted undertaking to date (Volkswagen Anhui, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330) was accepted precisely on those terms. In the absence of an adequate undertaking, the definitive measures under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force until 31 October 2029.

As the Berlin round convenes, BYD reiterates its openness to a price-undertaking framework that is workable for both sides, while noting that our plug-in-hybrid models fall outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 and should remain so. We will continue serving European customers across our full range, including the newly delivered PHEV stock already in EU dealer channels.

Ahead of the third round of negotiations in Berlin on 25–27 January 2027, the Commission reaffirms that any price undertaking will be accepted only if it demonstrably offsets the subsidy-caused injury and offers a level of protection equivalent to the definitive duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. Each offer will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily on its own merits, in line with WTO rules and the undertaking guidance of 12 January 2026.

The Berlin senior-official round (25–27 January) delivered substantive progress: we completed a first technical exchange on MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework against our 12 January 2026 guidance criteria. Let me be precise — any undertaking must be objectively equivalent in protection to the 2024 definitive duties, WTO-compatible, and open to all exporters on non-discriminatory terms; there is no blanket extension of the Volkswagen Anhui precedent.
