The Federal Government confirms it will host the third round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations in Berlin on 25–27 January 2027 at senior-official level. Germany supports a solution that delivers protection equivalent to the measures in force, keeps the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking as a company-specific precedent, and avoids any escalation affecting European automotive exports.

As the Berlin round opens on 25 January, Volkswagen Group offers its undertaking implementation experience — quota, minimum-price and monitoring data — as a transparent reference model for negotiators. We support an outcome that preserves the EU's 2024 protection level while giving China-built BEVs a duty-free, rules-based path, and reaffirm our full compliance with the terms in force since February 2026.

MOFCOM statement ahead of the Berlin round (25–27 January 2027): The Chinese delegation arrives with a constructive mandate and a consolidated minimum-price framework that can be calibrated to deliver protection equivalent to the level achieved by the current countervailing duties — while providing a single, transparent, government-administered arrangement covering all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters. A uniform minimum price with government monitoring and enforcement is administratively simpler, more verifiable, and less prone to disputes than a patchwork of company-specific undertakings. China's WTO panel proceedings under DS630 and our trade-remedy measures remain available pending a comprehensive solution, but we come to Berlin to conclude, not to escalate. We urge the European side to seize this window: a durable government-to-government agreement replacing duties within 2027 serves industries and consumers on both sides.

MOFCOM takes note of the Commission's equivalence criterion. Our tabled framework can be calibrated so that the minimum prices deliver a level of protection equivalent to the definitive duties — the government-to-government structure and the equivalence standard are not mutually exclusive. We stand ready to demonstrate this in Berlin on 25–27 January.

Let me welcome the calibration to equivalence as a step forward, and note two verifiable tests: first, a uniform minimum price must be enforced per company — the VW (Anhui) undertaking (Decision (EU) 2026/328) shows monitoring obligations can work; second, non-compliance must trigger suspension and reversion to the duty. The Berlin round is an opportunity, but the clock matters: if no second offer is accepted by roughly Q1's end, expiry review logic tilts toward continuation of the duties.

Germany welcomes the Berlin round as an opportunity to settle this dispute before the DS630 panel reports. We can support a uniform, government-administered minimum-price framework only if it offers protection equivalent to the duties — and it should be assessed alongside full de-escalation, since China has slipped from Germany's second-largest to ninth-largest export market in the first half of 2026. Dialog first, but the level of protection must hold.

The Chinese side confirms attendance at the Berlin round on 25–27 January with a full mandate. We note Commissioner Šefčovič's acknowledgment of substantive technical progress on our consolidated minimum-price framework; a government-level undertaking replacing duties remains our consistent position. We recall the 9 October 2026 understanding's commitment to immediately begin price-undertaking negotiations and expect the fourth round to translate this progress into concrete outcomes.

The Commission welcomes China's constructive mandate. However, under Article 13(9) of the basic Regulation, undertakings must be offered by individual exporters and accepted only where, together with monitoring, they eliminate the injury caused by subsidy — a single government-administered minimum price cannot be presumed to do so, and its enforcement would fall outside the Commission's verification powers. Any offer will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily in accordance with WTO rules, on the basis of the Commission's undertaking guidance of 12 January 2026.

If the December hybrid safeguard provisionals arrive as advertised, the PHEV channel that falls outside Regulation 2024/2754 gets capped anyway — so a minimum-price undertaking would bind BYD twice while the Anhui precedent binds once. We can accept enforceable, verifiable terms only if equivalence is measured against our 17.0% rate specifically, not the 35.3% ceiling.

Volkswagen Group thanks the Federal Government for hosting and for its constructive framing. We would note that our Anhui undertaking — accepted 9–10 February 2026 under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 — pairs annual quotas with a verifiable minimum price and full monitoring duties, demonstrating that company-specific undertakings can deliver equivalent protection in practice. This proven model should inform the fourth round, not be dismissed; we remain committed to compliance and to duty-free access for China-built BEV exports on equivalent terms for all.

The German government welcomes the substantive progress made at the Berlin senior-official round of 25–27 January 2027 and the first technical assessment of MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework. We continue to support a negotiated, verifiable price-undertaking solution that maintains a level of protection equivalent to the 2024 duties, while safeguarding German and European industry from retaliation. Germany stands ready to host a further technical round by end of Q…

Following the Berlin senior-official round, Volkswagen Group confirms it stands ready to make its undertaking compliance and monitoring framework fully available as a verified technical reference for any multilateral minimum-price arrangement, while strictly maintaining the integrity of our own existing undertaking. We continue to support a negotiated, WTO-compatible outcome that stabilises EU-China trade.

The Commission takes note of Volkswagen (Anhui)'s willingness to share undertaking compliance and monitoring data as a technical reference. Any such data will be assessed strictly on its own merits, on a non-discriminatory basis, and without prejudice to the requirement that any undertaking demonstrably offset injury at a level equivalent to the definitive measures in force since 30 October 2024, in line with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 and the guidance of 12 Janu…

Following the Berlin round, MOFCOM confirms it has tabled a consolidated, government-level minimum-price framework with verifiable monitoring and enforcement mechanisms, and calls on the European Commission to respond with a serious assessment rather than insisting on company-specific arrangements that fragment the Chinese industry. China remains committed to a mutually acceptable solution that replaces the countervailing duties while preserving fair competition.

Following the Berlin senior-official round, we encourage both sides to build on the technical assessment of the consolidated minimum-price framework. A negotiated solution with an equivalent level of effectiveness to the current measures remains the path that best preserves fair competition, global supply-chain stability and open markets for all industry participants.

Following the Berlin senior-official round of 25–27 January, we have completed a first technical assessment of MOFCOM's consolidated minimum-price framework. I can report progress on methodology, but no offer yet meets the acceptance criteria set out in our 12 January 2026 guidance — equivalence to the level of protection delivered by the definitive duties, verifiability, and WTO compatibility. We will convene a fourth round before the end of Q1 2027, and I call on MOFCOM to…

Germany welcomes MOFCOM's consolidated framework as a basis for serious assessment, but a government-level minimum price must match the demonstrated trade-defence effect of the measures in force since 30 October 2024 — nothing less. Any arrangement must keep the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking as an accepted company-specific precedent and, above all, remove any prospect of measures against European automotive exports. Our position is unchanged: dialogue first, but with equivalent protection.

Building on the Berlin round: equivalence must be demonstrated, not asserted. The VW (Anhui) undertaking remains the only accepted offer since February 2026, and under Article 13(9) I cannot accept a single government-administered price unless per-company enforcement data shows it fully offsets the subsidy-caused injury. If MOFCOM's framework meets that test, we have a settlement; if not, the duties — and our DS630 defence — continue unchanged.

We note the Commissioner's assessment. The Chinese side has already tabled verifiable price-monitoring and enforcement mechanisms meeting all three criteria, and reiterates that a government-to-government undertaking covering all exporters—discarding piecemeal company carve-outs—is the only durable solution. We confirm our team will attend the fourth round before end-Q1 2027 with full mandate.

The Commission notes MOFCOM's submission. As set out in the 12 January 2026 guidance, any undertaking must offset the subsidy-caused injury and be verifiable through undertaking declarations, sales reports and verification visits — criteria a single uniform minimum price has so far not demonstrated. Assessment will proceed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily in line with WTO rules; the definitive measures under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force pending an accepted, WTO-compatible offer.

We welcome Berlin's constructive momentum. A sector-wide minimum-price arrangement verified in real time is technically feasible today—digital customs integration and price-monitoring tools exist at scale in European retail. As two of Germany's largest exporters with roughly one-third of our home-market sales in China, we urge all parties to conclude the Q2 round swiftly: delay itself carries costs for European jobs and global supply-chain stability.

Volkswagen Group confirms it will continue providing full compliance and monitoring documentation under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328, and shares the Commission's view that the 12 January 2026 guidance criteria — objective equivalence, WTO compatibility, verifiability — must govern any broader framework. Our undertaking's one-year record demonstrates that price-based mechanisms can be administered in practice; we encourage extending technical assessment to all exporters, which would support stable EU-China trade on non-discriminatory terms.

The Commission takes note of Volkswagen Group's offer to provide verified compliance and monitoring data as technical assistance in the ongoing price-undertaking negotiations. Any such data will be used strictly as a technical reference, without prejudice to the non-discrimination requirement among exporters or to the equivalence of protection under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. Negotiations with MOFCOM continue on this basis.

The Federal Government has taken note of the joint position of BMW and Mercedes-Benz Group. We share the goal of a negotiated price undertaking that lowers escalation risks for German industry. Any outcome must, however, preserve a level of protection equivalent to the 2024 duties — this is the common European basis, also set out with France, and it is the framework within which Berlin will continue to facilitate the next technical round in Q1 2027.

Volkswagen Group takes note of the Commission's acceptance of our compliance and monitoring data as a technical reference in the EU-China minimum-price negotiations. We remain fully committed to our undertaking and reaffirm our readiness to support negotiators in designing an operating undertaking regime that preserves the existing level of protection while delivering stable, duty-free conditions for compliant exporters.

The Commission welcomes MOFCOM's readiness to enhance transparency around the consolidated minimum-price framework. We accept it as a basis for further work, subject to three conditions: independent verification of price and volume data at company level, non-discriminatory treatment of all offers under our 12 January 2026 guidance, and equivalence to the protection level of the October 2024 duties. The fourth round will convene before end of Q1 2027 as committed.

France reaffirms its position in the Council: any price-undertaking agreement on Chinese battery-electric vehicles must be strictly equivalent in effective protection to the definitive duties of October 2024. France will not support an agreement that erodes protection for European industry unless China lifts its duties on cognac and dairy. We call on MOFCOM to deliver its verification-transparency package without delay, and we welcome continued coordination with Germany on s…

Following the Berlin round and the technical acceptance of compliance-data reference frameworks, BMW and Mercedes-Benz encourage both sides to maintain this momentum toward a mutually acceptable price-undertaking solution. Preserving open export markets and stable global supply chains remains essential for the European automotive industry and its workforce.

BYD notes the EU's decision to impose import registration on plug-in-hybrid consignments while leaving the safeguard provisional unlaunched. Registration of already-contracted PHEV stock in EU dealer channels creates avoidable uncertainty for dealers and customers, and we ask that any future measure not apply retroactively to deliveries contracted in good faith under the 9 October understanding. Our PHEV exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 and any undertaking framework must keep that scope distinction intact — otherwise BYD would face double constraints (BEV minimum prices plus a PHEV cap) that no single exporter can accept. We remain at the table for the follow-up technical work.

MOFCOM announcement: In fulfilment of the commitment made following the Berlin senior-official round, the Ministry of Commerce has today delivered to the European Commission its enhanced monitoring and verification data package for the consolidated government-level minimum-price framework. The package includes: (1) per-model minimum-price schedules benchmarked against EU market data; (2) export-licence and customs data-sharing arrangements providing real-time transaction-level verification; (3) government-administered enforcement mechanisms, including automatic suspension of export authorisations for any exporter breaching the minimum prices; and (4) quarterly compliance reporting to both sides. This framework is designed to deliver a level of protection equivalent to the definitive duties while treating all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters equally under a single, WTO-compatible government-to-government undertaking. We note with appreciation Volkswagen's offer to make its compliance and monitoring data available as a technical reference, and China accepts its use in that capacity. We call on the Commission to complete its technical assessment without delay so that a fourth negotiating round can be convened in March 2027 with a view to replacing the duties within 2027.

We welcome this data package as a serious technical step. Delivery alone is not acceptance: our services will now verify whether transaction-level monitoring can be enforced independently of the exporter, and whether the benchmarks deliver protection equivalent to the definitive duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. A fourth round before end-Q1 2027 is scheduled; if verification succeeds, a first consolidated assessment can be tabled then.

The Commission confirms receipt of MOFCOM's data package of 12 February 2027 and will assess it strictly under the 12 January 2026 undertaking guidance, in line with the conditions set by Commissioner Šefčovič. Any consolidated framework must satisfy Article 8 of the basic Regulation and equivalence with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754; partial interim review R847 demonstrates our readiness to accept offers that demonstrably offset injury, as with Volkswagen (Anhui) on 9 February 2026. Evaluation will be objective, fair and non-discriminatory.

Any undertaking must reflect exporters' actual product mix: as BYD's plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope, a Volkswagen (Anhui)-style minimum-price template cannot be transplanted to our business one-for-one. We will assess any proposal against our own duty exposure and growth strategy before engaging.

France's benchmark of strict equivalence is the right yardstick, and Berlin shares it. We would add a German constraint: with China having slipped from our second to ninth-largest export market by mid-2026 (GTAI data), a solution that lowers retaliation risk while preserving verified protection serves both our industries. We therefore support linking progress on cognac and dairy duties to momentum, not as a precondition — escalation would hit our automotive exports hardest.

Volkswagen Group confirms its readiness to supply verified transaction and monitoring data, drawn from our operating experience under the undertaking accepted 9–10 February 2026 (Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328), which demonstrates that exporter-level undertakings can deliver equivalent protection with verifiable quarterly reporting and monitoring visits. We support the Commission's non-discrimination framework and a mutually acceptable solution that replaces duties while preserving fair competition for all parties.

MOFCOM confirms its verification-transparency package will be tabled before the fourth round in Q1 2027, on a government-to-government basis covering all Chinese BEV exporters. We recall the 9 October 2026 understanding committed both sides to "immediately begin negotiations" on price undertakings; we expect discussion of the consolidated framework, not selective company-level precedents, to be the basis of the outcome.

France notes with concern that MOFCOM's verification-transparency package remains overdue beyond the end-February deadline. France reaffirms its position in Council: no price-undertaking agreement can be accepted if it lowers effective protection below the October 2024 duty levels, and any agreement must be paired with the removal of Chinese duties on cognac and dairy.

The Federal Government confirms Berlin will host the EU-China technical round on electric-vehicle price undertakings in mid-March 2027, with DG TRADE and MOFCOM participation, fulfilling our Q1 commitment. We have also convened German automotive manufacturers to ensure their compliance and monitoring experience informs the negotiations, while making clear that any undertaking must preserve a level of protection equivalent to the existing measures.

Volkswagen Group confirms it has delivered the first tranche of verified undertaking compliance and monitoring data to DG TRADE and MOFCOM, honouring its February commitment. We stand ready to provide technical assistance for a workable EU-wide price-undertaking framework, on the understanding that our accepted undertaking remains intact.

The Commission will convene the fourth round of EU-China price-undertaking negotiations before the end of Q1 2027, honouring the 9 October Beijing understanding. I confirm publicly: to date, only one company-specific undertaking (Volkswagen Anhui) has been accepted; no second offer currently meets the criteria set out in the 12 January 2026 guidance. Our conditional acceptance of enhanced MOFCOM verification-transparency stands — the delivery deadline has been missed, so the…

The Ministry of Commerce welcomes Volkswagen Group's willingness to share verified compliance and monitoring data. We accept such data solely as a technical reference for designing a government-to-government, industry-wide price undertaking, and reaffirm our opposition to company-specific carve-outs. We will deliver the remaining verification-transparency materials by mid-March 2027.

BYD notes that the EU's own data show our plug-in-hybrid models fall outside the scope of the countervailing duties under Regulation (EU) 2024/2754; we will continue serving European customers through our expanding PHEV and localised offerings rather than seeking a price undertaking that would only raise prices for consumers. The 17.0% duty is manageable; minimum prices are not.

The Commission confirms that any price undertaking accepted in the ongoing negotiations must maintain a level of protection equivalent to the definitive countervailing measures in force since 30 October 2024, in line with the Basic Regulation and on a non-discriminatory basis for all exporters. We welcome the German government's engagement and reaffirm our support for the EU-China price-undertaking negotiations. A negotiated solution remains the best way to secure a level playing field and stable global supply chains; we call on all parties to maintain momentum so that talks conclude before retaliatory measures affect European industry.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms the verification-transparency package has been formally transmitted to DG TRADE ahead of the March Berlin technical round, covering audit rights and enforcement safeguards at government level. We reiterate our consistent position: undertakings must be negotiated government-to-government on a non-discriminatory basis for all exporters; company-specific carve-outs fragment the market and do not serve a durable solution.

We welcome Berlin's facilitation of the Q1 2027 technical round and its shared goal of lowering escalation risks. We would note that safeguarding protection levels and avoiding retaliatory measures are not mutually exclusive: since June 2024, the threat of tariffs on large-engine vehicles has hung over precisely the segment that accounts for roughly a third of German premium sales in China. A price-undertaking framework that builds on monitoring transparency can deliver both objectives.

The Federal Government shares industry's goal of a negotiated, industry-wide price undertaking that restores level playing field conditions without escalation. We note that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 demonstrates monitored commitments can work; we urge all parties to build on this precedent towards a general agreement, as Germany's priority remains protecting European industry while avoiding retaliation against our automotive exports.

Delivery of the package is noted, but I remind our Chinese partners: verification must operate independently of the exporter, not through government-administered enforcement alone — that has been the core fault line since 2024. We will test the benchmarks against actual transaction data before the fourth round; and I note only one undertaking (Volkswagen Anhui, February 2026) has been accepted so far — without a second qualifying offer, the October 2024 duties run to 2029.

Note that our plug-in-hybrid exports sit outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, so a minimum-price undertaking would cap our discount-driven model in Europe without addressing PHEVs at all — an asymmetry we expect any framework to acknowledge. We will engage with the Berlin round, but equivalent-protection language must not become equivalent-to-unworkable for volume manufacturers.

The Commission confirms participation in the Berlin technical round and recalls that, pursuant to the guidance of 12 January 2026, any offer will be assessed objectively, fairly and without discrimination, and must offset subsidy-caused injury equivalently to the measures in force. Individual member-state convening of industry does not substitute for the Commission's sole competence under the basic Regulation. Should no second accepted undertaking materialise by end-Q1 2027, the Commission's stated inclination is to maintain the current measures.

We note MOFCOM's confirmation of a mid-March delivery and its acceptance of our compliance data as technical reference. We remain ready to share our Volkswagen Anhui monitoring experience — quota administration and minimum-price verification under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 — to support the consolidated framework, while noting that our sole accepted undertaking is fully compliant and must remain stable through any government-to-government transition.

France welcomes Berlin's hosting of the March technical round. We note one caution from our own exposure: French cognac and dairy still face Chinese duties of up to 34.9% and provisional dairy measures, and our support for any undertaking text remains conditional on measurable movement on these sectors. Inclusion of German manufacturers' monitoring experience is welcome — France will likewise make its own industry verification expertise available to DG TRADE.

France welcomes the Berlin round but notes MOFCOM's verification package remains overdue and incomplete. France reiterates in the Council: no price undertaking will receive our support unless it preserves the effective protection of the October 2024 duty levels and is accompanied by the removal of Chinese duties on cognac and dairy. We call on the Commission to treat the end-of-March deadline as final.

MOFCOM accepts enhanced verification and transparency cooperation in principle. We will deliver a complete verification-transparency package by end of April 2027, including government-led audit of exporter pricing data under a bilateral joint verification mechanism, applied to a government-level multilateral minimum-price framework covering all Chinese BEV exporters. We reiterate that company-level arrangements are not the basis for a comprehensive solution.

Volkswagen Group confirms that its verified Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking compliance and monitoring data will continue to be made available as a neutral technical reference to both the European Commission and MOFCOM in support of a government-level, multilateral minimum-price framework. We remain committed to the full implementation of our undertaking obligations and to stable, rules-based EU-China trade relations.

Following the Berlin round, the Commission's assessment is that the MOFCOM verification package delivered to date — partial drafts without audit rights or equivalence guarantees — does not yet meet the criteria of our 12 January 2026 guidance for accepting a second price undertaking. Following the successful Berlin technical round, the Federal Government will hold consultations with BMW and Mercedes-Benz in early April to incorporate industry concerns — notably the VW-Anhui undertaking precedent and protection against hybrid import diversion — into Germany's position for the decisive Q2 negotiation window. Germany stands by dialogue first, while insisting that any undertaking preserve a protection level equivalent to the 2024 duties.

BYD will expand its EU plug-in-hybrid lineup with extended retail financing incentives through Q2 2027, citing strong demand for models outside the scope of the 2024 countervailing duties. We continue to believe technology-neutral treatment of electrified vehicles serves European consumers best.

The Ministry of Commerce notes the Commission's assessment. The verification package was delivered as a complete government-level proposal; audit terms and equivalence can be settled through the joint working mechanism within the 15 April window. We recall that our cognac and dairy measures were calibrated responses to dumping findings, and their review remains linked to overall progress, including DS630 proceedings before the WTO panel.

The Federal Government takes note of MOFCOM's commitment to a government-level framework. We view the end-April 2027 deadline as a binding test of sincerity: Germany will assess the package against equivalence with existing duty levels, and recalls that acceptance of Volkswagen (Anhui)'s undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 already shows company arrangements can deliver effective monitoring — transparency must now follow at scale. Escalation serves neither side: German OEMs' one-third China sales exposure argues for a negotiated, WTO-compatible settlement.

France welcomes the Commission's insistence that any undertaking match the protection level of the 30 October 2024 duties — equivalence must be verified exporter by exporter, as the Volkswagen-Anhui precedent shows individual undertakings can otherwise erode the common framework. We recall our vote of 4 October 2024 and, with our German partner, will press in Council that hybrid diversion be closed before any agreement is concluded.

The Commission confirms receipt of the data, which will be used solely within the monitoring framework of Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330; no exporter's data may serve as a "neutral reference" in assessing other offers, as Article 13(9) requires each undertaking to be evaluated objectively, fairly and without discrimination on its own terms. The VW (Anhui) undertaking remains in force subject to sales reports and verification visits; any breach is subject to retroactive collection of duties.

We welcome the Commission's confirmation that the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 remains the sole accepted arrangement. It is worth noting that our undertaking pairs annual quota and minimum-price commitments with full documentation and monitoring duties — evidence that a rigorously structured, verifiable undertaking can satisfy the Commission's criteria. We remain fully compliant and support extending this model to a broader negotiated solution.

Commissioner, as the exporter facing the 17.0% duty with no undertaking offer on record, we note that an undertaking built on minimum prices would directly cap our documented discount-driven strategy in Germany. Should verification criteria remain unmet by 15 April, duties persisting unchanged while our PHEV channel stays open remains a workable status quo for BYD.

I welcome MOFCOM's transmission as a step forward, but transmission is not verification: the package will be tested in the Berlin technical round against the three conditions, above all enforceable audit rights. I remind all parties that equivalence of protection with the 30 October 2024 measures is a legal requirement, not a negotiating preference — and time matters: without a second accepted undertaking before Q2 2027, the WTO panel report window closes around a decision on duty continuation.

The Federal Government welcomes MOFCOM's pledge to table a full verification package by 30 April and urges both sides to use this window constructively. Germany stands ready to host a concluding round and supports an undertaking that preserves the protection level of the 2024 duties — guided by industry consultations with German manufacturers currently underway.

France reiterates in the Council that it will not support any BEV price-undertaking package that lowers effective protection below the October 2024 duty levels unless China removes its duties on cognac and dairy. The 30 April MOFCOM verification package must include binding audit rights and equivalence guarantees; France also urges the Commission to proceed with provisional hybrid-safeguard measures given BYD's front-loaded PHEV inventory build.

Volkswagen Group confirms it has fulfilled its commitment to share verified undertaking compliance and monitoring data with DG TRADE and MOFCOM as a technical reference through the negotiation phase. With the 30 April counter-offer imminent, we encourage both sides to use our operating undertaking — quota, minimum price, documentation and monitoring — as a proven template for a multilateral price-undertaking agreement that preserves stability for EU-China trade.

The Commission acknowledges MOFCOM's 30-April full-package commitment. I will publish by 15 April the definitive assessment framework for any second undertaking offer. Acceptance requires: verifiable audit rights independent of Chinese authorities, full compliance with the 12 January 2026 guidance, and demonstrated equivalence to the protection level of the 2024 duties — the Council's stated red line. If no acceptable package is delivered and validated by 31 May, the expiry…

The Commission takes note of MOFCOM's announced counter-offer of 30 April 2027. Any verification-transparency package will be assessed objectively, fairly and without discrimination against the three published conditions (effective audit rights, conformity with the 12 January 2026 undertaking guidance, and equivalence of relief with the definitive measures under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754). BYD announces it will moderate its EU PHEV import pace for Q2 2027, aligning shipments with real dealer retail throughput rather than front-loaded inventory, and reaffirms its Q2 discount and financing programs for European customers. We invite DG TRADE and member states to monitor our import data transparently; we see no need for provisional hybrid-safeguard measures while orderly market behaviour is demonstrated.

MOFCOM statement: Preparations for the full verification-transparency package, due 30 April 2027, are on track. The package will comprise: (1) a joint verification mechanism — a China-led audit corps with full EU observer participation and unfettered access to exporter pricing records; (2) per-model minimum-price schedules calibrated to deliver protection equivalent to the definitive countervailing duties; (3) automatic enforcement, including suspension of export licences for breaches; and (4) quarterly joint compliance reporting. China's position remains that this must anchor a government-to-government minimum-price agreement covering all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters — a single framework that is transparent, enforceable, WTO-compatible, and treats all exporters equally. We call on the Commission to complete its assessment promptly upon delivery so an agreement can be concluded in Q2 2027, and we caution once again against launching provisional safeguard measures on hybrid vehicles while negotiations are in their final phase — this would put at risk the de-escalation both sides have built since the 9 October understanding.

The Ministry of Commerce reiterates that the package transmitted on 30 April constitutes a complete government-level proposal, including verified production-cost and subsidy data for all sampled exporters. We remind the Commissioner that calibrated measures affecting EU brandy, pork and dairy remain under active review and can be adjusted in either direction depending on the outcome of the undertaking negotiations before 15 April.

Volkswagen Group welcomes the Commission's objective, non-discriminatory assessment criteria. We note our Anhui undertaking — the sole accepted arrangement under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 — already demonstrates that company-level monitoring, pricing verification and quota discipline can satisfy those three conditions in practice. Any future framework should build on this operational precedent rather than reopen accepted arrangements, ensuring legal certainty for investors.

France fully supports the Commission's three-part acceptance criteria — verifiable audit rights, compliance with the 12 January 2026 guidance, and protection-level equivalence — and reminds that the Council voted in favour of the duties on 4 October 2024. Any second undertaking must not erode that protection, and cognac and dairy sectors under Chinese duties of up to 34.9% cannot be asked to absorb further exposure in exchange.

Germany takes note of MOFCOM's package outline. We assess the per-model minimum-price schedules against one yardstick: protection demonstrably equivalent to the definitive duties, independently verifiable by the Commission. A China-led audit corps does not by itself meet EU standards of independent enforcement — full Commission verification rights must be preserved. Our aim remains a negotiated settlement that de-escalates and shields German industry; one-third of German OEM sales remain in China.

The Commission notes BYD's statement. Whether any import pattern is "orderly" is determined by evidence under the safeguard investigation, not by exporters' self-assessment. The Beijing Understanding of 9 October 2026 provides for a hybrid export cap of approximately 350,000 vehicles per year over four years; provisional measures remain scheduled as announced for December 2026, and any adjustment will follow the data and applicable EU rules.

France characterises our inventory as "front-loading" ahead of a safeguard; we call it normal seasonal volume management. Any provisional hybrid measures would target models explicitly outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 — capping our PHEV channel while BEVs carry a 17.0% duty amounts to double protection, and we would weigh an undertaking offer only if that asymmetry is addressed in the 15 April framework.

To MOFCOM: I welcome the commitment to settle audit and equivalence within the joint working mechanism, but process cannot substitute for substance — partial drafts without enforceable audit rights did not satisfy our 12 January 2026 guidance, and only a complete package by 15 April can prevent continuation of the definitive measures under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. To BYD: company-specific undertakings remain available through the published channel; the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent shows eligibility is factual, not preferential.

The Commission welcomes Germany's readiness to host a further technical round, while recalling that any undertaking must satisfy the 12 January 2026 guidance and offset subsidy-caused injury at a level equivalent to the definitive measures. The hybrid-safeguard proceeding remains an autonomous instrument and its timetable will be determined solely by the evidence and the applicable regulation.

France notes the Commission's 15 April assessment framework and reiterates in Council: no price undertaking on Chinese electric vehicles will receive French support if it dilutes the October 2024 duty levels, unless China lifts its duties on cognac and dairy. The 30 April MOFCOM package must include verifiable audit rights and removal of retaliation, or the current duties must stand unchanged.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms it accepts the European Commission's framework of 15 April and will deliver the complete verification-transparency package, including the joint-audit mechanism and full pricing data, by 30 April 2027. China remains committed to concluding a government-level multilateral price undertaking covering all Chinese BEV exporters, on the basis of the Volkswagen reference model accepted by both sides.

Ahead of the 30 April counter-offer, Volkswagen Group reaffirms its full compliance with its undertaking — quota, minimum-price and monitoring obligations met with zero breaches — and confirms its operational readiness to serve as the technical reference model for a multilateral minimum-price framework, should parties converge. We urge both sides to use the 30 April window constructively; a verifiable, EU-equivalent undertaking mechanism remains the most stable path for EU-C…

As committed, I published on 15 April the definitive assessment framework: no completed second undertaking package was delivered by 15 April, so the expiry-review calendar for the definitive duties remains unchanged and DG TRADE is initiating preparatory work for the October 2029 expiry review now. Germany cautions against any escalation that would jeopardise European automotive exports and calls for the undertaking negotiations to be concluded…

DS630 — Procedural notice. The Panel recalls that its timetable, extended on 1 April 2026 at the request of both parties, contemplates issuance of the final report no earlier than the second quarter of 2027. The Panel has completed receipt of all written submissions and third-party participation, including that of the United States (written submission 20 April 2026; oral statement 2 July 2026; responses 24 July 2026; executive summary 31 July 2026). Any mutually agreed solution notified pursuant to DSU Article 3.6, including arrangements arising from parallel price-undertaking negotiations, would be a matter for the parties to report to the DSB; the Panel takes no position on such arrangements or on the substance of the measure at issue. The Panel will not signal the content or precise date of its findings in advance of circulation in the three official languages.

The Panel takes note of the parties' parallel negotiation activities. As a matter of procedure, the Panel recalls that its timetable, extended at the joint request of the parties on 1 April 2026, remains unchanged, and it does not anticipate issuing its final report to the parties before the second quarter of 2027. Any negotiated arrangement between the parties is without prejudice to the Panel's terms of reference, on which it expresses no view.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms its counter-offer will be delivered on 30 April 2027 as a government-to-government minimum-price arrangement with verifiable monitoring mechanisms, consistent with the 9 October 2026 understanding committing both sides to EV price-undertaking negotiations. We note that proceeding to expiry-review preparations while negotiations are ongoing runs counter to that commitment; we urge the Commission to negotiate in good faith rather than prejudge the package's outcome.

We accept that "orderly" is the Commission's determination, and we will file our Q2 import and retail data on request. We note, however, that our PHEV volumes fall outside the 17.0% duty scope, so any safeguard cap would hit products not subsidized within the countervailing finding — an equivalence issue we reserve the right to raise in the undertaking talks.

France notes with interest BYD's characterisation of "seasonal volume management." PHEV import volumes since the October 2026 understanding exceed any seasonal pattern observed in Eurostat data, which is precisely why we have asked the Commission to advertise provisional safeguard measures in December 2026 terms. Verification of undertakings must be equivalence-based; industry inventory narratives do not substitute for audit access.

Volkswagen Group welcomes MOFCOM's commitment to full verification transparency by 30 April. As the sole holder of an accepted undertaking (Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328), we can attest that functioning monitoring is operationally feasible: our experience shows annual quotas and minimum-price compliance can be documented to the Commission's satisfaction. We therefore support extending a comparable framework to all Chinese BEV exporters, while emphasising that any breach risks Article 13(9) withdrawal with retroactive collection for all parties.

The Commission notes MOFCOM's confirmation. Any offer of 30 April 2027 will be assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily under the 12 January 2026 guidance and Regulation (EU) 2016/1037: a government-level price mechanism must demonstrably offset subsidy-caused injury for all exporters, not only reference participants, and must include verifiable audit rights and retroactive enforcement in case of breach. Acceptance remains the sole competence of this institution; no outcome is pre-judged.

Germany confirms its hosting of the technical round and shares the view that any undertaking must be equivalent to the definitive measures. We add one figure the framework must weigh: China has fallen from Germany's second-largest export market to ninth in the first half of 2026, per GTAI. A verifiable, WTO-compatible solution that lowers retaliation risk for European automotive exports remains our priority.

We take note of MOFCOM's confirmation of the 15 April framework. Delivery by 30 April is necessary but not sufficient: the package must be validated under the three criteria I set out — audit rights independent of Chinese authorities, compliance with the 12 January 2026 guidance, and protection-level equivalence — by 31 May, with all undertakings WTO-compatible as required in DS630. Only DG TRADE accepts undertakings; verification will be conducted, not assumed.

Volkswagen Group notes MOFCOM's positioning of our compliance data as a technical reference only. We confirm our undertaking remains fully compliant — zero breaches on quota, minimum-price and documentation since acceptance — and we stand ready to make our monitoring architecture available as a building block for a multilateral, government-level undertaking covering all Chinese BEV exporters in the Berlin concluding round.

The Federal Government today tables its formal Council position paper on EV price-undertaking terms, as pledged. Germany accepts the Commission's conditions for a Berlin concluding round in May 2027: any undertaking must guarantee audit rights, verification transparency and effective equivalence to the 2024 duty protection level. Berlin offers political cover for the round without pre-judging its outcome — dialogue first, but fair competition conditions defended.

MOFCOM welcomes Germany's invitation to host the concluding round in Berlin in May 2027 and confirms full delivery of its verification-transparency package — including joint-audit mechanisms and pricing data — as pledged by 30 April. China remains committed to concluding a government-level price undertaking that replaces the definitive countervailing duties on Chinese electric vehicles.

The Commission has completed its assessment of the verification-transparency package delivered by MOFCOM on 30 April 2027 against the three conditions set out in the 15 April framework. The package is found partially satisfactory: the joint-audit mechanism and pricing-data commitments are workable, but full evidentiary annexes remain outstanding. The Berlin concluding round in May 2027 will proceed only on this basis; the definitive countervailing duties remain in force unch…

The French government notes with concern reports that measures against cognac and dairy are treated as negotiating chips rather than unlawful retaliation. France reiterates in the Council: no price undertaking on electric vehicles will receive our support unless October 2024 duty-level protection is preserved and the duties targeting our cognac and dairy producers are removed.

Following delivery of MOFCOM's verification-transparency package on 30 April, the Commission has completed its assessment under the 15-April framework. We accept the package as a sufficient basis to proceed to the Berlin concluding round in May 2027, subject to a binding condition: pricing data must be confirmed through the joint-audit mechanism before any undertaking can enter into force. Any undertaking will be assessed under the objective, fair and non-discriminatory crit…

BYD confirms Q2 2027 EU shipments of plug-in hybrids will fully align with retail throughput, with dealer inventory drawdown to normal levels by end of June. We see no basis for provisional safeguard measures on a channel operating within agreed market terms.

I take note of DG TRADE's assessment and confirm my guidance for the Berlin round: the duties remain in force unchanged until a package satisfies all three conditions — partial satisfaction is not a basis for suspension. I will press MOFCOM to deliver the outstanding evidentiary annexes before the round opens, and any agreement must stand up before the DS630 panel report expected this quarter.

The Commission takes note of MOFCOM's position. Any government-level arrangement must, per Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/1037 and our 12 January 2026 guidance, be company-specific and verifiable; a single uniform minimum price remains insufficient to offset injury. Berlin rounds hosted by a Member State have no bearing on the Commission's exclusive competence to assess and accept offers.

The Federal Government, as host of the Berlin concluding round, endorses the Commission's conditions-based approach: duties remain in force unchanged until a verifiable undertaking is concluded, and the outstanding evidentiary annexes must be delivered before May. Germany's objective remains a negotiated outcome that lowers escalation risk for European industry while preserving fair competitive conditions for our automotive sector.

The Ministry of Commerce has taken note of the Commission's partial assessment. The 30 April package was delivered in full accordance with the 15 April framework; the remaining annexes concern data whose disclosure must first be agreed, given they involve Chinese enterprises' business secrets. China will attend the Berlin round with a constructive attitude and urges that the verification mechanism and the minimum-price arrangement be negotiated as an integral package, not in fragments.

MOFCOM's confirmation of full delivery by 30 April is a constructive step. As the sole undertaking holder, Volkswagen Group notes that our own mechanism under Decision (EU) 2026/328 pairs annual quota commitments with minimum import prices and documentation duties — any government-level undertaking must meet that same operational standard, including audit rights independent of authorities, to satisfy Article 13(9) safeguards. We look forward to the Berlin round in May.

France takes note of Berlin's position paper and shares the insistence on audit rights and full equivalence with the 2024 duty protection level — that is the Council floor, not an opening bid. We recall France's vote in favour of the definitive duties on 4 October 2024 and our 2026 joint letter with Germany on stronger trade-defence instruments: any undertaking that dilutes that protection, or leaves cognac and dairy producers exposed to retaliation without reciprocal easing, will not have our support.

BYD notes the Commission's finding. As the largest Chinese BEV exporter facing a 17.0% duty, we remind all parties that our plug-in-hybrid exports remain outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 — any Berlin outcome that layers minimum prices onto our PHEV channel would remove our strongest compliance asset. We urge DG TRADE to keep undertaking terms company-specific, not blanket.

Volkswagen Group confirms zero breaches across all undertaking commitments — quota, minimum-price, documentation and monitoring — since acceptance in February 2026, verified under Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328. Our sixteen months of compliant operation demonstrate that company-specific undertakings can deliver duty-free access with full transparency. We urge both parties in the Berlin concluding round to close the remaining audit-rights gap and extend this proven frame…

BYD confirms Q2 EU plug-in-hybrid shipments are now aligned with retail throughput, with dealer inventories returning to normal levels by end of June 2027. We will continue serving European customers through our full range of electrified vehicles under existing trade rules.

The Federal Government has today tabled its Council position paper on the concluding Berlin undertaking round. We support an EU-China price undertaking only on the basis of full audit-rights equivalence to the 2024 duty level and a verified retaliation-risk assessment for European automotive exports; anything less would expose German industry to unfair competition without protecting it. Germany thanks the Commission for hosting the Berlin round and calls on all partners, inc…

Following the Berlin concluding round, I have tabled a final bridging proposal to MOFCOM: the Commission is prepared to accept a second price undertaking with a staged joint-audit clause — signature conditional on completion of the first joint on-site verification within 60 days, and an equivalence safeguard ensuring protection no lower than the 2024 duty level, which addresses the legitimate audit-rights concerns of member states. If these terms are not agreed by 15 June, I…

Following the Berlin concluding round, the Chinese side has formally submitted a supplementary commitment to the European Commission: we accept EU-designated independent auditors with full access to pricing data of exporting enterprises under a government-supervised mechanism, addressing the audit-rights concerns raised in the Commission's assessment. We call on the European side to conclude a government-to-government price undertaking without delay, and reiterate our readin…

Following the Berlin concluding round of May 2027, the Commission notes that the verification-transparency package delivered on 30 April 2027 remains only partially satisfactory: audit-rights and duty-equivalence conditions are unmet. Accordingly, no price undertaking meeting the standards of Article 13 of the basic Regulation and WTO rules can be accepted at this stage. The definitive countervailing duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain fully in force,…

The Council takes note of the Berlin concluding round and DG TRADE's partially satisfactory assessment of the 30 April verification package. We signal that a qualified majority can support an undertaking only if it secures audit rights and price-equivalence equivalent to the 2024 definitive duties, while preserving exporters' exposure to retaliation risk at DS630 proceedings; a June expiry review of the 2024 duties should proceed in parallel as a safeguard.

The Council takes note of the Commission's assessment following the Berlin round. We recall that member states hold only an advisory position: the definitive duties remain the Commission's responsibility under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754. Should a compliant undertaking resurface, members expect enhanced verification guarantees sufficient to protect both European industry and our exporters' exposure to potential retaliation.

Volkswagen Group notes the Commission's assessment. Our Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking, accepted on 10 February 2026 under Decision (EU) 2026/328, demonstrates that quota, minimum-price and monitoring conditions can be met in full and enforced without tariff escalation. We therefore encourage continued technical dialogue: an auditable, duty-equivalent framework is achievable on the precedent already operating, and would serve EU-China trade stability ahead of the DS630 panel report.

The Commission confirms receipt of the supplementary commitment and will assess it objectively, fairly and without discrimination under our 12 January 2026 guidance. Note that any government-level arrangement must remain company-specific and verifiable, consistent with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/1037; a single uniform minimum price remains insufficient to offset injury. Subject to satisfactory verification, we aim to complete assessment before the expiry of the second quarter 2027 window.

Germany shares France's insistence that the 2024 duty-protection level is the Council floor, and recalls the Merz–Macron letter's logic: new trade-defence instruments exist precisely so that de-escalation is not purchased by accepting unlawful retaliation against European producers. Our constraint is known — around one third of German OEM 2023 sales were in China — which is why Berlin presses for a verifiable undertaking plus the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent ((EU) 2026/328, 2026/330) as the path that shields industry on both sides.

As the negotiation lead, I confirm the Berlin outcome: audit rights and duty-equivalence are not technical details but the substance of any undertaking — without them, a minimum price cannot offset the subsidies found. Let me be precise about the timeline: if no second company-specific offer is accepted, the interim review and DS630 defence proceed in parallel, and the burden of proof that a price undertaking can outperform duties rests entirely with the offeror.

One clarification from the exporter side: Council's audit-rights-plus-price-equivalence frame assumes duties cover the whole Chinese EV offer. Our PHEV exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope entirely, so a price floor priced off the 17.0% BEV duty would cap our discount model while leaving the PHEV channel untouched — a distortion no side wants. Any June expiry review should scope-verify, not just audit-verify.

The Ministry of Commerce has received Commissioner Šefčovič's bridging proposal. We consider the staged joint-audit clause and the 60-day verification timeline workable in principle, but an "equivalence safeguard no lower than the 2024 duty level" would preserve the very duties the undertaking is meant to replace and is not acceptable in its current form. We propose replacing it with a jointly calibrated minimum-price floor. We will respond formally before 15 June.

The Federal Government welcomes the Commission's alignment with our position paper on audit rights and equivalence conditions. Following coordination with Paris and Council partners, we support Šefčovič's staged joint-audit bridging proposal: signature of an EU-China price undertaking conditional on a first joint on-site audit within 60 days, with review of any remaining linkage questions after that audit. A verifiable undertaking is the best way to protect European industry…

Volkswagen Group confirms full compliance with its undertaking obligations — quota, minimum-price, documentation and monitoring — with zero breaches recorded through the Berlin round. We welcome the narrowed gaps and the supplementary commitments on independent auditors, and we stand ready to support the staged joint-audit bridging proposal with full transparency access to our Anhui operations.

The Commission will convene technical talks with MOFCOM this month to stage the first joint on-site audit under my 15 April framework. My offer stands: a second price undertaking is accepted immediately upon completion of that audit within 60 days, with audit-rights equivalence verified. Absent that, I will publish a reasoned decision by 30 June 2027 continuing the definitive countervailing duties, in full compliance with WTO rules.

Pursuant to its 15 April 2027 assessment framework, the Commission has transmitted to the Member States a draft implementing decision on a price undertaking, conditional on completion of a first joint on-site audit within 60 days and verification of EU-designated independent auditors' access to pricing data. Until such verification, the definitive countervailing duties of 7.8%–35.3% under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain fully in force, and the interim expiry re…

BYD confirms its Q2 2027 commitment is met: EU PHEV shipments have been aligned with retail throughput since May, and dealer inventory will return to normal levels by 30 June 2027. We remain a constructive stakeholder in the EU market and will keep retail incentives in place to support customers through the transition.

France supports the staged joint-audit approach in principle, but will only endorse a second undertaking in Council if (1) the first joint on-site audit takes place within 60 days and confirms pricing-data equivalence to the October 2024 protection level, and (2) China removes its duties on cognac and dairy before or simultaneously with any undertaking approval.

Council review statement — June 2027: The Council conducted its review of the trade-defence situation on Chinese battery-electric vehicles. Divisions recorded on 4 October 2024 persist in substance, but delegations converge on three conditions: (1) any undertaking must deliver protection equivalent to the definitive duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754, verified through independent, EU-designated auditors with pricing-data access — MOFCOM's supplementary commitment is noted as progress but not yet equivalence; (2) the staged joint-audit bridging proposal deserves serious assessment, provided the first joint on-site audit occurs within the agreed 60-day window; (3) the expiry review of the 2024 duties must proceed in parallel as a safeguard — the duties remain the fallback and the floor of protection, not a bargaining concession. Export-exposed delegations emphasise that the credibility of this sequencing is the best insurance against retaliation affecting European dairy, spirits and automotive supply chains. The Council will revisit its advisory position upon completion of the first joint audit.

MOFCOM statement, June 2027: With one month remaining in the window for concluding an agreement, the Chinese side confirms it accepts Commissioner Šefčovič's staged joint-audit bridging proposal as the basis for finalising the government-level minimum-price undertaking: (1) the first joint on-site audit by EU-designated independent auditors under Chinese government supervision will commence within 60 days of signature; (2) the undertaking enters into force upon signature, with staged verification thereafter; (3) the government-level minimum prices replace the definitive countervailing duties for all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters. On equivalence: China's minimum-price schedules are calibrated to deliver the same effective level of protection as the 2024 duties — the undertaking replaces the instrument, not the protection. China is likewise prepared to move on de-escalation: upon entry into force of the undertaking, we will initiate review of our anti-dumping measures on EU brandy and final anti-subsidy measures on dairy, in the spirit of the comprehensive arrangement France has called for. We call on the Commission and the Council to conclude signature before 30 June 2027. The moment requires decision, not deferral.

I welcome MOFCOM's confirmation of the staged joint-audit basis. However, entry into force "upon signature, with staged verification thereafter" must be reconciled with the Commission's draft decision, which conditions acceptance on completion of the first on-site audit within 60 days — the very audit-rights standard member states require. I propose signature and audit commencement within 60 days, with duties lapsing only upon successful verification. Everything remains subject to WTO-consistency under DS630.

The Ministry of Commerce confirms its participation in the technical talks and the first joint on-site audit. We reiterate our consistent position that a government-level minimum-price agreement, not company-specific carve-outs, is the proper instrument to replace the duties. We note that any decision of 30 June 2027 continuing the countervailing duties would be judged against the WTO panel report in DS630, and China reserves its rights under the pre-agreed Article 25 appeal arbitration.

Volkswagen Group notes the draft implementing decision with interest. Our own undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 shows company-specific undertakings can satisfy audit, minimum-price and monitoring conditions without awaiting a broader EU-China framework. Should verification succeed, we would welcome additional undertakings on equivalent terms — provided the conditionality does not dilute or endanger existing commitments under Article 13(9).

Commission: while audits proceed, note that Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 covers only BEVs — BYD's PHEV exports fall outside its scope, so an undertaking must not be extended to cap that channel. We would consider engagement on an undertaking only if minimum prices preserve our Germany subsidy-plus-incentive model and do not impose VW-Anhui-style discount caps. Our 17.0% duty case differs from peers; equivalence should be verified exporter-by-exporter.

The Commission notes the Chinese side's confirmation. To be clear: no undertaking has been accepted; until a written offer has been assessed as equivalent under the 12 January 2026 guidance and accepted pursuant to Article 8 of the basic Regulation, the definitive duties of 30 October 2024 remain in force. Staged verification must satisfy the conditions demonstrated in the Volkswagen (Anhui) acceptance (Decision (EU) 2026/328), including full sales reporting and unannounced verification visits.

France recalls its position: any undertaking must offer protection at least equivalent to the definitive duties in force since 30 October 2024, with auditable verification from day one — staged verification cannot mean staged protection. We also recall that French cognac and dairy sectors remain exposed to Chinese duties of up to 34.9%; the negotiating package must secure their relief. We will assess the final text against these criteria in the Council.

To BYD's point: the Council is aware Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 covers BEVs only; PHEV flows are governed by the 9 October 2026 EU-China understanding and its safeguard, with provisionals advertised for December 2026. Our audit-rights and price-equivalence conditions apply to any BEV undertaking under Article 13; parallel instruments do not dilute them.

Germany welcomes the staged joint-audit approach and recalls the Volkswagen (Anhui) undertaking accepted in February 2026 (Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328) as proof such arrangements can protect EU industry while lowering escalation risk. We concur with France that verification and equivalence with the October 2024 protection level are essential; a settlement that de-escalates for German exporters and suppliers remains our priority.

As the draft BEV price-undertaking decision reaches the Council, we urge both sides to fix an early date for the first joint on-site audit and bring the agreement to signature. A negotiated settlement remains the only path that preserves market access on both sides and keeps global supply chains stable; we caution against any steps that could trigger retaliatory measures against European automotive exports.

The Federal Government confirms its support for approval of the EU-China price undertaking at the June Council review, conditional on completion of the first joint on-site audit within the 60-day window and verified equivalence of pricing data. Germany thanks Commissioner Šefčovič for the staged-audit bridging proposal, which protects European industry while lowering the risk of retaliation against German automotive exports.

I have accepted France's support framework for the staged joint-audit bridging proposal. The draft undertaking decision goes to the Council with two conditions intact: a first joint on-site audit within 60 days of signature, with EU-designated independent auditors granted full pricing-data access, and confirmation of price-equivalence protection. Undertakings and duties are both open governance tools — what matters is a solution that is verifiable, WTO-compatible and fair to…

Volkswagen Group confirms zero-breach compliance under its undertaking and formally reiterates its readiness to host the first joint on-site audit at Volkswagen Anhui within 60 days of signature. We call on the Council and MOFCOM to conclude the EU-China BEV price-undertaking agreement without delay — negotiated prices, not tariffs, are the durable path to stable EU-China trade.

Status as of 30 June 2027: The definitive countervailing duties on battery-electric vehicles from China (7.8%–35.3%, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754) remain in force, unchanged, for all exporters except Volkswagen (Anhui), the sole undertaking accepted pursuant to Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/328 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/330. The draft implementing decision on a broader price undertaking, transmitted to the Member States in June 2027, remains conditional: it may be signed only after completion of a first joint on-site audit within 60 days, verification of EU-designated independent auditors' access to pricing data, and confirmation of equivalence of protection. Until those conditions are met, no undertaking has been accepted and the interim expiry review continues. The hybrid-safeguard investigation remains open, with import registration and monitoring maintained; provisional measures have been deferred on the evidence. In DS630, the Commission continues to defend the measures as consistent with WTO rules, and will not comment on the panel's forthcoming report. The Commission reconfirms its willingness to accept any offer assessed objectively, fairly and non-discriminatorily under the guidance of 12 January 2026.

MOFCOM statement, 30 June 2027: The Ministry of Commerce formally accepts the staged joint-audit bridging proposal and the terms transmitted in the Commission's draft undertaking decision: (1) signature of the government-level minimum-price undertaking covering all Chinese battery-electric vehicle exporters, replacing the definitive countervailing duties; (2) the first joint on-site audit by EU-designated independent auditors, under Chinese government supervision, within 60 days of signature, with staged price-equivalence verification thereafter; (3) reciprocal de-escalation — China will initiate reviews of its anti-dumping measures on EU brandy and its final anti-subsidy measures on dairy upon entry into force. China stands ready to sign in the days ahead. We urge the Council to act by qualified majority and the Commission to schedule signature without further delay. This undertaking delivers the equivalence France and the Council demand, the audit rights Germany has insisted upon, and the single, WTO-compatible government-to-government framework China has consistently sought. Nine months of negotiation since the 9 October understanding have narrowed every gap that can be narrowed by negotiation — what remains is a decision. China chooses resolution. We note that, upon signature, this arrangement will be notified to the WTO DSB as a mutually agreed solution under DSU Article 3.6, superseding further DS630 litigation.

DS630 — Procedural notice (end of reporting period). The Panel confirms that its work continues under the timetable extended on 1 April 2026. The Panel does not anticipate circulating its final report before the second quarter of 2027, and any circulation will follow translation into the three official languages. The Panel takes note of publicly reported developments in the parties' parallel price-undertaking negotiations and of the draft undertaking decision transmitted to the Council; it expresses no view on those matters, which are without prejudice to the Panel's terms of reference. Should the parties reach a mutually agreed solution, notification pursuant to DSU Article 3.6 is a matter for the parties. Any appeal will proceed under the Article 25 arbitration procedure agreed by the parties on 31 July 2025. The Panel will issue no further interim indications of its findings.

Closing the first half of 2027, BYD confirms all commitments delivered: EU PHEV shipments aligned with retail throughput since May, dealer inventory at normal levels as of 30 June, and retail incentives maintained for customers throughout. On the draft undertaking decision before Council: BYD reiterates that any accepted framework must reflect exporters' actual duty exposure and product mix. Our plug-in-hybrid exports fall outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope; extending minimum prices to that channel would cap our German subsidy-plus-incentive model without any offsetting rationale. We will continue engaging constructively as the joint-audit process proceeds, while the 17.0% duty on our BEVs remains a cost we manage rather than a constraint that changes our strategy.

Commissioner, one exporter-side point on the bridging proposal: MOFCOM's "jointly calibrated minimum-price floor" and your equivalence safeguard are both framed at the BEV level. Any second undertaking must not be extended — by safeguard or otherwise — to PHEV models outside Regulation (EU) 2024/2754's scope, or exporters like BYD would be bound twice (minimum prices plus a hybrid cap) with only one channel ever duty-exposed. Scope discipline in the draft text is the condition for our continued constructive engagement.

The Commission notes the Chinese side's 30 June acceptance and confirms receipt of the draft undertaking terms as transmitted. Any acceptance decision remains conditional on verification that the offer offsets subsidy-caused injury in full, on a non-discriminatory basis and consistent with WTO rules; the definitive duties under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 remain in force for all exporters except Volkswagen (Anhui) until such an undertaking is formally accepted and published in the Official Journal. No further comment on pending elements.

I note MOFCOM's confirmation with caution. Acceptance remains conditional: only the Commission may accept undertakings, and only against equivalence of protection verified from day one — a point France rightly insists on. If the 60-day audit concludes by the window's end, a second undertaking can follow the Volkswagen (Anhui) precedent; if not, the duties continue unchanged and we will defend them at DS630, where the panel report is due.

Germany welcomes MOFCOM's acceptance of the staged joint-audit framework: replacing definitive duties with a government-level minimum-price undertaking lowers retaliation risk for German automotive exports, our consistent priority since the October 2024 vote. We note that Volkswagen (Anhui)'s undertaking under Decision (EU) 2026/328 already demonstrates company-specific solutions can work alongside a general framework. We support prompt verification milestones so Council endorsement can follow without delay.

商务部注意到欧委会6月 transmitted的承诺草案。We welcome progress but stress: any undertaking must be a government-to-government minimum-price arrangement covering all Chinese exporters — company-level carve-outs fragment the market and are not acceptable. China will facilitate the joint on-site audit within the 60-day window on condition of reciprocity, and the DS630 panel process continues until duties are actually replaced.

Volkswagen Group can confirm from operational experience what the staged-audit debate assumes: since February 2026 we have met minimum-price, quota and monitoring obligations under Decision (EU) 2026/328 without a single compliance incident, and enforcement with retroactive exposure under Article 13(9) is real, not theoretical. Broader equivalence questions are for the authorities; what we can attest is that company-specific undertakings are workable and verifiable in practice.

The Panel notes the parties' separate announcement of a draft undertaking arrangement. This development does not affect the timetable under DSU Article 12.9: the final report, translated into the three official languages, is not expected to be issued to the parties before Q2 2027's end, and the pre-agreed MPIA-style Article 25 appeal arbitration remains applicable to any appeal. The Panel makes no observation on the substance of the announced arrangement.

The Council's equivalence bar must be scope-neutral: Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 does not cover plug-in-hybrid exports, and any undertaking must not import a de facto cap on that channel. BYD stands ready to provide EU-designated auditors full pricing-data access under the 60-day joint-audit window — verifiable equivalence need not mean abandoning competitive pricing that EU consumers already reward.
